title.zh: 卷三百二十一 列傳第二百〇九 外國二 安南
title.raw: 卷三百二十一 列傳第二百〇九 外國二 安南 Volume 321 Biographies 209: Foreign States 2 - Annan

sentences.zh: 安南，古交阯地。

translations.literal: Annan was the ancient territory of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Annan was the old land of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 唐以前皆隸中國。

translations.literal: Before the Tang, it was entirely subordinate to China.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Tang dynasty, it was wholly under Chinese administration.

sentences.zh: 五代時，始為土人曲承美竊據。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period, the native Qu Chengmian first seized it by force.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, a local leader named Qu Chengmian first wrested control of the region.

sentences.zh: 宋初，封丁部領為交阯郡王，三傳為大臣黎桓所篡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, Ding Bo Linh was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaozhi Commandery; after three generations a great minister, Le Huan, usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, Ding Bo Linh was invested as Prince of Jiaozhi; three reigns later the senior minister Le Huan seized power.

sentences.zh: 黎氏亦三傳為大臣李公蘊所篡。

translations.literal: The Le house also passed through three generations before the great minister Li Gongyun usurped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Le clan likewise held power for three generations until the senior minister Li Gongyun overthrew them.

sentences.zh: 李氏八傳，無子，傳其婿陳日炬。

translations.literal: The Li line endured eight generations; having no son, the throne passed to his son-in-law Chen Rijiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Li family ruled for eight generations; when the line died without a male heir, rule passed to the son-in-law Chen Rijiu.

sentences.zh: 元時，屢破其國。

translations.literal: In Yuan times, [the court] repeatedly broke their state.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, the imperial armies repeatedly crushed the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 以寧等至，日煃先卒，侄日熞嗣位。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yining and the others arrived, Chen Ri Kui had already died, and his nephew Chen Ri Xiao succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Zhang Yining and his party reached Annan, Chen Ri Kui was already dead, and his nephew Chen Ri Xiao had taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 遣其臣阮汝亮來迎，請誥印，以寧等不予。

translations.literal: [Ri Xiao] sent his minister Ruan Ruliang to welcome them and request the patent and seal; Yining and the others did not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his minister Ruan Ruliang to receive the envoys and request investiture and the royal seal, but Yining and his colleagues refused.

sentences.zh: 日熞乃復遣杜舜欽等請命於朝，以甯駐安南俟命。

translations.literal: Ri Xiao then again sent Du Shunqin and others to seek investiture at court, and had Ning remain in Annan awaiting the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Ri Xiao then dispatched Du Shunqin and others to petition the court for recognition, while keeping Yining in Annan to await the imperial response.

sentences.zh: 時安南、占城構兵，帝命翰林編修羅復仁、兵部主事張福諭令罷兵，兩國皆奉詔。

translations.literal: At that time Annan and Champa were at war; the Emperor ordered Hanlin Compiler Luo Furen and Ministry of War Principal Clerk Zhang Fu to instruct them to cease fighting, and both states obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Annan and Champa were then at war; the Emperor ordered the Hanlin compiler Luo Furen and the Ministry of War clerk Zhang Fu to command both sides to lay down arms, and both kingdoms complied.

sentences.zh: 明年，舜欽等至告哀。

translations.literal: The next year, Shunqin and the others arrived to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shunqin and his party arrived to report the bereavement.

sentences.zh: 帝素服禦西華門引見，遂命編修王廉往祭，賻白金五十兩、帛五十匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor, in plain garb, received them at the West Hua Gate, then ordered Compiler Wang Lian to go perform the sacrifice, with condolence gifts of fifty taels of white silver and fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received them in mourning dress at the West Hua Gate, then sent the compiler Wang Lian to conduct the rites of mourning, with fifty taels of silver and fifty bolts of silk as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 別遣吏部主事林唐臣封日熞為王，賜金印及織金文綺紗羅四十匹。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched Ministry of Personnel Principal Clerk Lin Tangchen to invest Ri Xiao as king, granting a gold seal and forty lengths of brocaded gauze and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Lin Tangchen of the Ministry of Personnel to invest Ri Xiao as king, bestowing a gold seal and forty lengths of gold-woven silk and gauze.

sentences.zh: 廉既行，帝以漢馬援立銅柱鎮南蠻，厥功甚偉，命廉就祀之。

translations.literal: After Lian had set out, the Emperor, reflecting that the Han general Ma Yuan had erected the Bronze Pillar to pacify the southern barbarians—a feat of great merit—ordered Lian to offer sacrifice there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lian was on his way, the Emperor recalled how the Han general Ma Yuan had set up the Bronze Pillar to subdue the southern tribes, a deed of great renown, and ordered Lian to worship at that site as well.

sentences.zh: 尋頒科舉詔于其國，且以更定嶽瀆神號及廓清沙漠，兩遣官詔告之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the civil-service examination edict was promulgated in that country, and, moreover, because the designations of the sacred mountains and rivers had been revised and the desert had been pacified, officials were twice dispatched to proclaim these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the examination edict was issued in Annan, and when the court revised the titles of the sacred mountains and rivers and celebrated the pacification of the desert, envoys were sent twice to announce these changes.

sentences.zh: 日熞遣上大夫阮兼、中大夫莫季龍、下大夫黎元普等謝恩，貢方物。

translations.literal: Ri Xiao sent Senior Grand Master Ruan Jian, Grand Master Mo Jilong, Junior Grand Master Li Yuanpu, and others to express gratitude and present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Ri Xiao sent Senior Grand Master Ruan Jian, Grand Master Mo Jilong, Junior Grand Master Li Yuanpu, and others to offer thanks and present tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 兼卒於道，詔賜其王及使臣，而送兼柩歸國。

translations.literal: Jian died on the road; an edict granted rewards to the king and the envoys, and Jian’s coffin was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died en route; the court ordered gifts for the king and the mission, and had Jian’s coffin escorted back to Annan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復仁等還，言卻其贐不受，帝嘉之，加賜季龍等。

translations.literal: Before long Furen and the others returned, reporting that they had refused bribes offered them; the Emperor commended this and added further gifts for Jilong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luo Furen and his party returned, reporting that they had declined gifts pressed upon them; the Emperor praised their conduct and ordered additional rewards for Jilong and the others.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遣使貢象，賀平沙漠，復遣使隨以寧等來朝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year [of Hongwu], [Annan] sent envoys presenting elephants to congratulate [the court] on pacifying the desert, and again sent envoys who followed Yining and the others to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Annan sent tribute elephants to congratulate the court on pacifying the desert, and again dispatched envoys who came to court with Yining’s party.

sentences.zh: 其冬，日熞為伯父叔明逼死。

translations.literal: That winter, Ri Xiao was forced to his death by his uncle Shuming.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Ri Xiao was driven to his death by his uncle Chen Shuming.

sentences.zh: 叔明懼罪，貢象及方物。

translations.literal: Shuming, fearing punishment, presented elephants and local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing imperial punishment, Shuming sent elephants and other tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 逾年至京，禮官見署表非日熞名，詰得其實，詔卻之。

translations.literal: More than a year later they reached the capital; the ritual officials saw that the memorial bore a name other than Ri Xiao’s, questioned them, and learned the truth; an edict rejected the tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the capital more than a year later, the ritual officials noticed the memorial was not signed in Ri Xiao’s name; once the facts were established, the court ordered the tribute turned away.

sentences.zh: 叔明復朝貢謝罪，且請封。

translations.literal: Shuming again came to court with tribute to beg forgiveness and also to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming again sent tribute to court to beg forgiveness and to request formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 其使者抵言日熞實病死，叔明遜避於外，為國人所推。

translations.literal: His envoys, on arrival, declared that Ri Xiao had in fact died of illness, that Shuming had withdrawn in humility, and that the people of the state had pressed him forward.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys claimed on arrival that Ri Xiao had truly died of illness, that Shuming had modestly withdrawn, and that the people had urged him to take power.

sentences.zh: 帝命國人為日熞服，而叔明姑以前王印視事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the people of the state to observe mourning for Ri Xiao, while Shuming was for the time being to conduct state affairs with the former king’s seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the people of Annan to mourn Ri Xiao, while allowing Shuming to govern provisionally with the former king’s seal.

sentences.zh: 七年，叔明遣使謝恩，自稱年老，乞命弟耑攝政，從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Shuming sent envoys to express gratitude, saying he was old and begging that his younger brother Ri He be appointed to govern; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shuming sent envoys to give thanks, saying he was aged and asking that his younger brother Ri He be appointed regent; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 耑遣使謝恩，請貢期。

translations.literal: Ri He sent envoys to express gratitude and to request a schedule for tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Ri He sent envoys to offer thanks and to ask when tribute missions should be sent.

sentences.zh: 詔三年一貢，新王世見。

translations.literal: An edict fixed tribute once every three years, with a new king appearing in person at his investiture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed tribute at once every three years, requiring a new king to appear in person at investiture.

sentences.zh: 尋復遣使貢，帝令所司諭卻，且定使者毋過三四人，貢物無厚。

translations.literal: Soon [Annan] again sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to instruct them to turn back, and also fixed that envoys should not exceed three or four persons and that tribute goods should not be lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Annan sent tribute again; the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to tell them to withdraw, and limited missions to no more than three or four envoys with modest gifts.

sentences.zh: 十年，耑侵佔城，敗沒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Ri He invaded Champa and was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Ri He attacked Champa and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 弟煒代立，遣使告哀，命中官陳能往祭。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wei succeeded him and sent envoys to announce mourning; the Emperor ordered the eunuch Chen Neng to go perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei took the throne and sent envoys to report the bereavement; the Emperor ordered the eunuch Chen Neng to conduct the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 時安南怙強，欲滅占城，反致喪敗。

translations.literal: At that time Annan, relying on its strength, wished to destroy Champa but instead brought defeat upon itself.
translations.idiomatic: Annan had grown overconfident and sought to destroy Champa, only to suffer a crushing reverse.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官諭前王叔明毋構釁貽禍，以叔明實主國事也，叔明貢方物謝罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched officials to instruct the former king Shuming not to provoke trouble and invite disaster, for Shuming in fact controlled state affairs; Shuming presented local products to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent officials to warn the former king Shuming not to stir up trouble, noting that Shuming still effectively ruled; Shuming sent tribute to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 廣西思明土官訴安南犯境，安南亦訴思明擾邊。

translations.literal: The native official of Siming in Guangxi reported that Annan had violated the border, and Annan in turn accused Siming of harassing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Siming native official in Guangxi complained that Annan had crossed the border, while Annan accused Siming of frontier harassment.

sentences.zh: 帝移檄數其奸誑罪，敕守臣勿納其使。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a proclamation enumerating their deceit and crimes and ordered frontier officials not to receive their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a proclamation listing their fraud and crimes and ordered border officials to refuse their missions.

sentences.zh: 煒懼，遣使謝罪，頻年貢奄豎、金銀、紫金盤、黃金酒尊、象馬之屬。

translations.literal: Wei, in fear, sent envoys to beg forgiveness and for several years presented eunuchs, gold and silver, purple-gold trays, golden wine vessels, elephants, horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wei sent envoys to apologize and for years sent tribute including eunuchs, gold and silver, purple-gold platters, golden wine cups, elephants, and horses.

sentences.zh: 帝命助教楊盤往使，令饋雲南軍餉，煒即輸五千石于臨安。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Instructor Yang Pan to go on a mission and to supply provisions for the Yunnan army; Wei immediately delivered five thousand piculs of grain to Lin’an.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent instructor Yang Pan as envoy and ordered Annan to supply the Yunnan army; Wei at once delivered five thousand piculs of grain to Lin’an.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，帝復命禮部郎中邢文偉齎敕及幣往賜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Emperor again ordered Ministry of Rites Director Xing Wenwei to carry an imperial letter and silks as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Emperor again sent Xing Wenwei of the Ministry of Rites with an imperial letter and gift silks.

sentences.zh: 煒遣使謝，復進象。

translations.literal: Wei sent envoys to express thanks and again presented elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys to give thanks and again offered elephants.

sentences.zh: 帝以其頻煩，且貢物侈，命仍三歲一貢，毋進犀象。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because [tribute] came too frequently and the gifts were extravagant, ordered tribute to remain once every three years and forbade the presentation of rhinoceros horn and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the missions too frequent and the gifts excessive, the Emperor restored the three-year tribute cycle and forbade rhinoceros horn and elephants.

sentences.zh: 時國相黎季犛竊柄，廢其主煒，尋弑之，立叔明子日焜昆主國事，仍假煒名入貢。

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Le Qui Li seized power, deposed his lord Wei, and soon murdered him; he installed Shuming’s son Ri Kun to manage state affairs, yet still sent tribute under Wei’s name.
translations.idiomatic: By then the chief minister Le Qui Li had seized power, deposed King Wei, and soon murdered him; he set Shuming’s son Ri Kun to govern while still sending tribute under Wei’s name.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知而納之，越數年始覺，命廣西守臣絕其使。

translations.literal: The court did not know this and accepted it; only after several years did they realize it, and ordered Guangxi frontier officials to cut off their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew nothing of this and accepted the missions; only years later did they discover the truth and order Guangxi officials to bar Annan’s envoys.

sentences.zh: 季犛懼，二十七年遣使由廣東入貢。

translations.literal: Qui Li, in fear, in the twenty-seventh year sent envoys to present tribute through Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Qui Li in the twenty-seventh year sent envoys to offer tribute through Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣宜詰責，卻其貢。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent envoys to rebuke and reject the tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged, sent officials to rebuke him, and refused the tribute.

sentences.zh: 季犛益懼，明年復詭詞入貢。

translations.literal: Qui Li grew still more afraid; the next year he again entered tribute with specious words.
translations.idiomatic: Qui Li grew more frightened still; the following year he again sent tribute with deceitful explanations.

sentences.zh: 帝雖惡其弑逆，不欲勞師遠征，乃納之。

translations.literal: Although the Emperor detested his regicide and usurpation, he did not wish to weary the armies with a distant campaign, and so accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor loathed his murder and usurpation, he was unwilling to dispatch armies on a distant expedition and therefore accepted the tribute.

sentences.zh: 大軍方討龍州趙宗壽，命禮部尚書任亨泰、御史嚴震直諭日焜，毋自疑。

translations.literal: The great army was then campaigning against Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou; the Emperor ordered Minister of Rites Ren Hengtai and Censor Yan Zhenzhi to instruct Ri Kun not to doubt [the court’s intentions].
translations.idiomatic: As the main forces were suppressing Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, the Emperor ordered Ren Hengtai and Yan Zhenzhi to assure Ri Kun that he need not fear the court.

sentences.zh: 季犛聞言，稍自安。

translations.literal: When Qui Li heard this, he was somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Qui Li heard this, he felt somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣刑部尚書楊靖諭令輸米八萬石，餉龍州軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent Minister of Justice Yang Jing to order the delivery of eighty thousand piculs of grain to supply the Longzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent Yang Jing of the Ministry of Justice to demand eighty thousand piculs of grain for the Longzhou army.

sentences.zh: 季犛輸一萬石，饋金千兩、銀二萬兩，言龍州陸道險，請運至憑祥洞。

translations.literal: Qui Li delivered ten thousand piculs and presented one thousand taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver, saying the overland route to Longzhou was perilous and asking that grain be transported to Pingxiang Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Qui Li sent only ten thousand piculs and offered one thousand taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver, pleading that the overland route to Longzhou was dangerous and asking that grain be shipped to Pingxiang Cave.

sentences.zh: 靖不可，令輸二萬石于沲海江，江距龍州止半日。

translations.literal: Jing would not agree and ordered twenty thousand piculs delivered to the Tuohai River, which was only half a day’s journey from Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing refused and ordered twenty thousand piculs delivered to the Tuohai River, only half a day from Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 靖因言：「日焜年幼，國事皆決季犛父子，乃敢觀望如此。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon said: “Ri Kun is young; state affairs are all decided by Qui Li father and son, yet they dare to hang back like this.”
translations.idiomatic: Jing reported: “Ri Kun is young and all affairs are decided by Qui Li and his son, yet they dare stall in this fashion.”

sentences.zh: 」時帝以宗壽納款，移兵征向武諸蠻，遂諭靖令輸二萬石給軍，而免其所饋金銀。

translations.literal: At that time, because Zongshou had submitted, the Emperor shifted troops to campaign against the Xiangwu tribes; he then instructed Jing to demand twenty thousand piculs for the army and exempted the gold and silver they had offered.
translations.idiomatic: As Zongshou had surrendered, the Emperor redirected troops against the Xiangwu tribes and told Jing to take twenty thousand piculs for the army while waiving the gold and silver offered.

sentences.zh: 明年，季犛告前王叔明之訃。

translations.literal: The next year, Qui Li reported the death of the former king Shuming.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Qui Li announced the death of the former king Shuming.

sentences.zh: 帝以叔明本篡弑，弔祭則獎亂，止不行，移檄使知之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that Shuming had originally usurped and murdered his lord, thought that condolence rites would reward rebellion and therefore did not perform them, sending a proclamation to make this known.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuming had originally usurped and murdered his sovereign, the Emperor held that mourning rites would reward rebellion and refused to perform them, notifying Annan by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 思明土官黃廣成言：「自元設思明總管府，所轄左江州縣，東上思州，南銅柱為界。

translations.literal: The Siming native official Huang Guangcheng said: “Since the Yuan established the Siming Pacification Commission, the prefectures and counties along the Left River that it governed had Shangsi Prefecture to the east and the Bronze Pillar as the southern boundary.”
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guangcheng, native official of Siming, stated: “Since the Yuan set up the Siming Pacification Commission, its Left River prefectures and counties were bounded on the east by Shangsi and on the south by the Bronze Pillar.”

sentences.zh: 元征交阯，去銅柱百里立永平寨萬戶府，遣兵戍守，令交人給其軍。

translations.literal: When the Yuan campaigned against Jiaozhi, they went a hundred li beyond the Bronze Pillar to establish the Yongping Stockade Myriad Households Office, garrisoned troops there, and ordered the people of Jiaozhi to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan attacked Jiaozhi they advanced a hundred li past the Bronze Pillar to establish the Yongping Stockade office, stationed troops there, and required the Jiaozhi people to provision the garrison.

sentences.zh: 元季喪亂，交人攻破永平，越銅柱二百餘里，侵奪思明所屬丘溫、如嶅、慶遠、淵、脫等五縣地，近又告任尚書置驛思明洞登地。

translations.literal: In the disorder at the end of the Yuan, the people of Jiaozhi broke Yongping and, advancing more than two hundred li beyond the Bronze Pillar, seized the five districts of Qiuwen, Ruyao, Qingyuan, Yuan, and Tuo that belonged to Siming; recently they had also claimed that Minister Ren had set up a courier station on Siming Cave Deng land.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yuan turmoil Jiaozhi forces overran Yongping and, pushing more than two hundred li past the Bronze Pillar, seized Siming’s districts of Qiuwen, Ruyao, Qingyuan, Yuan, and Tuo; they had lately also claimed Minister Ren had established a relay station on Siming’s Deng territory.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗具奏，蒙遣楊尚書勘實。

translations.literal: I have already memorialized in detail and was ordered to send Minister Yang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: I have already submitted a full memorial and the court sent Minister Yang to verify the facts.

sentences.zh: 乞敕安南以五縣地還臣，仍畫銅柱為界。

translations.literal: I beg that Annan be ordered to return the five districts to me and that the Bronze Pillar again be taken as the boundary.”
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Annan be ordered to return the five districts and that the Bronze Pillar again be fixed as the border.”

sentences.zh: 」帝命行人陳誠、呂讓往諭，季犛執不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the envoy Chen Cheng and Lü Rang to go instruct them; Qui Li obstinately refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent envoys Chen Cheng and Lü Rang to instruct Annan, but Qui Li stubbornly refused.

sentences.zh: 誠自為書諭日焜，季犛貽書爭，且為日焜書移戶部。

translations.literal: Cheng himself wrote a letter instructing Ri Kun; Qui Li sent a letter disputing it and also drafted a memorial for Ri Kun to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wrote personally to instruct Ri Kun; Qui Li replied with a disputing letter and even drafted a memorial for Ri Kun to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 誠等復命，帝知其終不肯還，乃曰：「蠻夷相爭，自古有之。

translations.literal: When Cheng and the others returned and reported, the Emperor knew they would never return the land and said: “Barbarians quarreling with one another is an affair as old as antiquity.”
translations.idiomatic: On their return the Emperor knew Annan would never restore the territory and said, “Barbarians fighting among themselves is nothing new.”

sentences.zh: 彼恃頑，必召禍，姑俟之。

translations.literal: “They rely on obstinacy and will surely invite disaster; let us wait for now.”
translations.idiomatic: “They trust in their stubbornness and will bring ruin upon themselves; we may wait for now.”

sentences.zh: 」建文元年，季犛弑日焜，立其子顒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen, Qui Li murdered Ri Kun and installed his son Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianwen reign Qui Li murdered Ri Kun and set up his son Yong.

sentences.zh: 又弑顒，立其弟案，方在繈褓中，復弑之。

translations.literal: He also murdered Yong and installed his younger brother An; while An was still in swaddling clothes, he murdered him as well.
translations.idiomatic: He then murdered Yong and set up his younger brother An; while An was still an infant in arms, he murdered him too.

sentences.zh: 大殺陳氏宗族而自立，更姓名為胡一元，名其子蒼曰胡，謂出帝舜裔胡公後，僭國號大虞，年號元聖，尋自稱太上皇，傳位，朝廷不知也。

translations.literal: He massacred the Chen clan and set himself up, changing his surname and personal name to Hu Yiyuan; he named his son Cang Hu Di, claiming descent from Emperor Shun’s descendant Lord Hu, usurped the state name Great Yu, adopted the reign title Yuansheng, soon styled himself Retired Emperor, and transferred power to Di—the court knew nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered the Chen clan and seized the throne, changing his name to Hu Yiyuan and naming his son Cang Hu Di, claiming descent from Lord Hu, scion of Emperor Shun; he usurped the title Great Yu, adopted the reign title Yuansheng, soon called himself Retired Emperor, and passed rule to Di—yet the court knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 思明所轄祿州、西平州、永平寨為所侵奪，帝諭令還，不聽。

translations.literal: The Luzhou, Xipingzhou, and Yongping Stockade under Siming’s jurisdiction were seized by them; the Emperor instructed them to return the territory, but they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou, Xipingzhou, and Yongping Stockade under Siming were seized; the Emperor ordered their return, but Annan refused.

sentences.zh: 占城訴安南侵掠，詔令修好。

translations.literal: Champa complained that Annan had raided and plundered; an edict ordered them to restore good relations.
translations.idiomatic: Champa complained of Annan’s raids; an edict ordered both sides to make peace.

sentences.zh: 陽言奉命，侵掠如故，且授印章逼為屬，又邀奪天朝賜物。

translations.literal: Di outwardly claimed to obey the command yet continued raiding as before, and moreover issued seals to compel submission, also intercepting gifts bestowed by the Heavenly Court.
translations.idiomatic: Di pretended to obey yet continued his raids, issued seals to force submission, and even seized gifts sent by the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，方遣官切責，而故陪臣裴伯耆詣闕告難，言：「臣祖父皆執政大夫，死國事。

translations.literal: The Emperor detested this and was just sending officials to rebuke him sharply when the former tributary official Pei Bozhe came to the capital to report his plight, saying: “My grandfather and father were both chief ministers who died in the service of the state.”
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was about to send a stern rebuke when former tributary official Pei Bozhe arrived at court to plead his case, saying, “My grandfather and father were both chief ministers who died serving the throne.”

sentences.zh: 臣母，陳氏近族。

translations.literal: “My mother was a close kinswoman of the Chen house.”
translations.idiomatic: “My mother was a near relative of the Chen clan.”

sentences.zh: 故臣幼侍國王，官五品，後隸武節侯陳渴真為裨將。

translations.literal: “Therefore, when young I attended the king and held a fifth-rank office; later I served Vice Military Commissioner Chen Kezhen as a deputy commander.”
translations.idiomatic: “As a boy I attended the king in a fifth-rank post; later I served Vice Military Commissioner Chen Kezhen as his deputy.”

sentences.zh: 洪武末，代渴真禦寇東海。

translations.literal: “At the end of the Hongwu reign I replaced Kezhen in defending against pirates on the eastern sea.”
translations.idiomatic: “At the end of the Hongwu era I replaced Kezhen in guarding the eastern coast against pirates.”

sentences.zh: 而賊臣黎季犛父子弑主篡位，屠戮忠良，滅族者以百十數，臣兄弟妻孥亦遭害。

translations.literal: “Then the traitorous minister Le Qui Li, father and son, murdered their sovereign and usurped the throne, slaughtering the loyal and good; those whose clans were exterminated numbered in the hundreds and tens, and my brothers, wives, and children also suffered.”
translations.idiomatic: “Then the traitor Le Qui Li and his son murdered the sovereign and usurped power, butchering the loyal; hundreds of families were wiped out, and my brothers, wives, and children perished as well.”

sentences.zh: 遣人捕臣，欲加誅醢。

translations.literal: “They sent men to capture me, intending to execute and dismember me.”
translations.idiomatic: “They sent men to seize me, intending to torture me to death.”

sentences.zh: 臣棄軍遁逃，伏處山谷，思詣闕庭，披瀝肝膽，輾轉數年，始睹天日。

translations.literal: “I abandoned my post and fled, hiding in mountain valleys, longing to reach the court and pour out my heart; after several years of hardship I finally saw the light of day.”
translations.idiomatic: “I fled my post and hid in the mountains, yearning to reach the capital and lay bare my heart; only after years of wandering did I behold the imperial sun.”

sentences.zh: 竊惟季犛乃故經略使黎國髦之子，世事陳氏，叨竊寵榮，及其子蒼，亦蒙貴任。

translations.literal: “I reflect that Qui Li is the son of the former pacification commissioner Le Guomao, who for generations served the Chen house and enjoyed favor and glory; his son Cang also received high office.”
translations.idiomatic: “Qui Li is the son of former pacification commissioner Le Guomao, whose family served the Chen for generations and enjoyed honor; his son Cang too held high office.”

sentences.zh: 一旦篡奪，更姓易名，僭號改元，不恭朝命。

translations.literal: “In a single day they usurped and seized power, changed their surnames and personal names, usurped titles and altered reign eras, and showed no respect for the court’s commands.”
translations.idiomatic: “In a single stroke they seized the throne, changed their names, usurped titles and reign eras, and defied the court.”

sentences.zh: 忠臣良士疾首痛心，願興吊伐之師，隆繼絕之義，蕩除奸凶，復立陳氏後，臣死且不朽。

translations.literal: “Loyal ministers and good officials gnash their teeth in grief and wish to raise punitive forces to restore the interrupted line of the Chen, to sweep away the traitors and re-establish a Chen heir; even in death I would not perish.”
translations.idiomatic: “The loyal gnash their teeth in anguish and long for punitive armies to restore the Chen line, sweep away the traitors, and set up a Chen heir; I would die content.”

sentences.zh: 敢效申包胥之忠，哀鳴闕下，惟皇帝垂察。

translations.literal: “I dare emulate Shen Baoxu’s loyalty and wail my appeal below the palace gates; may the Emperor look down in compassion.”
translations.idiomatic: “I dare follow Shen Baoxu’s example and cry out at the palace gates; may Your Majesty look upon me with pity.”

sentences.zh: 」帝得奏感動，命所司周以衣食。

translations.literal: The Emperor, moved on reading the memorial, ordered the relevant offices to supply him with clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to provide clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 會老撾送陳天平至，言：「臣天平，前王日烜孫，奣子，日煃弟也。

translations.literal: Just then Laos sent Chen Tianping, who said: “I, Tianping, am the grandson of the former king Ri Xuan, son of Yong, and younger brother of Ri Kui.”
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Laos presented Chen Tianping, who said, “I, Tianping, am grandson of the former king Ri Xuan, son of Yong, and younger brother of Ri Kui.”

sentences.zh: 黎賊盡滅陳族，臣越在外州獲免。

translations.literal: “The Le bandits exterminated the Chen clan; I alone escaped in a distant prefecture.”
translations.idiomatic: “The Le rebels exterminated the Chen house; I alone survived in a distant district.”

sentences.zh: 臣僚佐激于忠義，推臣為主以討賊。

translations.literal: “My retainers, stirred by loyalty and righteousness, urged me as lord to punish the rebels.”
translations.idiomatic: “My followers, moved by loyalty, urged me to lead them against the rebels.”

sentences.zh: 方議招軍，賊兵見迫，倉皇出走，竄伏岩穀，萬死一生，得達老撾。

translations.literal: “Just as we were recruiting troops, rebel soldiers pressed upon us; I fled in panic and hid in rocky valleys, escaping death by a hair’s breadth, and reached Laos.”
translations.idiomatic: “As we were raising troops the rebels closed in; I fled in terror to mountain caves, barely surviving, and reached Laos.”

sentences.zh: 恭聞皇帝陛下入正大統，臣有所依歸。

translations.literal: “I have heard that Your Majesty has entered upon the great succession; I have one to whom I may turn.”
translations.idiomatic: “I have heard that Your Majesty has ascended the throne; at last I have a sovereign to whom I may turn.”

sentences.zh: 匍匐萬里，哀訴明庭。

translations.literal: “Crawling ten thousand li, I come in grief to plead before the bright court.”
translations.idiomatic: “Having crawled ten thousand li, I come in sorrow to plead before the imperial court.”

sentences.zh: 陳氏後裔止臣一人，臣與此賊不共戴天。

translations.literal: “Of the Chen descendants I alone remain; I cannot live under the same sky as this bandit.”
translations.idiomatic: “I alone remain of the Chen line; I cannot share heaven with this traitor.”

sentences.zh: 伏祈聖慈垂憐，迅發六師，用章天討。

translations.literal: “I beg the sacred compassion to pity me and swiftly dispatch the Six Armies to manifest Heaven’s punishment.”
translations.idiomatic: “I beg Your sacred mercy to pity me and swiftly send the imperial hosts to execute Heaven’s judgment.”

sentences.zh: 」帝益感動，命所司館之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was still more moved and ordered the relevant offices to lodge him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved still more deeply and ordered that he be housed at court.

sentences.zh: 方遣使賀正旦，帝出天平示之，皆錯愕下拜，有泣者。

translations.literal: Di was then sending envoys to congratulate the New Year; the Emperor produced Tianping for them to see; all were startled and prostrated themselves, and some wept.
translations.idiomatic: Di had just sent envoys for the New Year audience; the Emperor displayed Tianping before them; all were stunned and bowed, and some wept.

sentences.zh: 伯耆責使者以大義，惶恐不能答。

translations.literal: Bozhe rebuked the envoys with righteous principle; they were terrified and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhe upbraided the envoys on grounds of righteousness; terrified, they could not reply.

sentences.zh: 帝諭侍臣：「父子悖逆，鬼神所不容，而國中臣民共為欺蔽。

translations.literal: The Emperor told his attendants: “Di father and son are rebellious and defiant; even ghosts and spirits cannot tolerate them, yet the ministers and people of the state together deceive and conceal the truth.”
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told his attendants, “Di and his father have rebelled against Heaven; even ghosts and spirits abhor them, yet the whole country joins in deceit.”

sentences.zh: 一國皆罪人也，朕烏能容。

translations.literal: “The entire state are criminals; how can I tolerate them?”
translations.idiomatic: “The whole kingdom are criminals; how can I spare them?”

sentences.zh: 」三年命御史李琦、行人王樞齎敕責，令具篡弑之實以聞。

translations.literal: In the third year he ordered Censor Li Qi and Envoy Wang Shu to carry an imperial letter rebuking Di and command him to report in full the facts of the usurpation and murder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he ordered Li Qi and Wang Shu to deliver an imperial rebuke demanding a full account of the usurpation and murders.

sentences.zh: 雲南寧遠州復訴侵奪七寨，掠其婿女。

translations.literal: Ningyuan Prefecture in Yunnan again reported that Di had seized seven stockades and carried off the daughter of a son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Ningyuan Prefecture in Yunnan again reported that Di had seized seven stockades and abducted a son-in-law’s daughter.

sentences.zh: 遣其臣阮景真從琦等入朝謝罪，抵言未嘗僭號改元，請迎天平歸，奉為主，且退還祿州、寧遠地。

translations.literal: Di sent his minister Ruan Jingzhen to follow Qi and the others to court to beg forgiveness, declaring on arrival that he had never usurped a reign title or altered an era name, asking to welcome Tianping home and install him as ruler, and promising to return Luzhou and Ningyuan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Di sent Ruan Jingzhen to accompany Qi’s party to court, claiming he had never usurped titles or changed reign eras, offering to welcome Tianping and restore him as king, and promising to return Luzhou and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝不虞其詐，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, not suspecting deceit, consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, unsuspecting treachery, agreed.

sentences.zh: 命行人聶聰齎敕往諭，言：「果迎還天平，事以君禮，當建爾上公，封以大郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Envoy Nie Cong to carry an imperial letter instructing them, saying: “If you truly welcome Tianping back and treat him with the rites due a sovereign, you shall be made Senior Duke and enfeoffed with a great commandery.”
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Nie Cong with an imperial letter stating: “If you truly restore Tianping and honor him as sovereign, you shall be made Senior Duke and granted a great fief.”

sentences.zh: 」復遣景真從聰等還報，迎天平。

translations.literal: Di again sent Jingzhen to return with Cong and the others to report and welcome Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Di again sent Jingzhen back with Cong’s party to confirm and escort Tianping home.

sentences.zh: 聰力言誠可信，帝乃冬天平還國，敕廣西左、右副將軍黃中、呂毅將兵五千送之。

translations.literal: Cong strongly urged that Di was truly trustworthy; the Emperor then sent Tianping home in winter and ordered the left and right deputy generals of Guangxi, Huang Zhong and Lü Yi, to lead five thousand troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong insisted Di could be trusted; that winter the Emperor sent Tianping home, ordering Huang Zhong and Lü Yi of Guangxi with five thousand troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 四年，天平陛辭，帝厚加賚，敕封順化郡公，盡食所屬州縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Tianping took leave at court; the Emperor richly rewarded him and ordered Di enfeoffed as Duke of Shunhua Commandery, with full revenue from his subordinate prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Tianping bid farewell at court; the Emperor lavished gifts upon him and invested Di as Duke of Shunhua, granting him all subordinate prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 三月，中等護天平入雞陵關，將至芹站，伏兵邀殺天平，中等敗還。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhong and the others escorted Tianping through Jiling Pass; as they neared Qin Station, Di’s ambush killed Tianping, and Zhong and the others were defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the escort entered Jiling Pass; near Qin Station Di’s ambush slew Tianping, and the Ming force was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，召成國公硃能等謀，決意討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged, summoned the Duke of Cheng, Zhu Neng, and others to deliberate, and resolved to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Emperor summoned Zhu Neng, Duke of Cheng, and others and resolved on war.

sentences.zh: 七月命能佩征夷將軍印充總兵官，四平侯沐晟佩征夷副將軍印為左副將軍，新城侯張輔為右副將軍，豐城侯李彬、雲陽伯陳旭為左、右參將，督師南征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he ordered Neng to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Yi and serve as commander-in-chief; the Marquis of Siping, Mu Sheng, wore the seal of Deputy General Who Pacifies the Yi as left deputy commander; the Marquis of Xincheng, Zhang Fu, as right deputy commander; the Marquis of Fengcheng, Li Bin, and the Earl of Yunyang, Chen Xu, as left and right staff generals—to supervise the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Neng was appointed commander-in-chief as General Who Pacifies the Yi; Mu Sheng, Marquis of Siping, was left deputy; Zhang Fu, Marquis of Xincheng, right deputy; Li Bin and Chen Xu staff generals—to lead the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 能至龍州病卒，輔代將其軍。

translations.literal: Neng reached Longzhou and died of illness; Fu took over command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Neng reached Longzhou and died; Fu assumed command.

sentences.zh: 入安南坡壘關，傳檄數一元父子二十大罪，諭國人以輔立陳氏子孫意。

translations.literal: Entering Annan through Polei Pass, he issued a proclamation enumerating twenty great crimes of Yiyuan father and son and instructed the people of the state of the court’s intent to restore a Chen descendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Polei Pass Fu issued a proclamation listing twenty crimes of the Hu father and son and announced the court’s aim to restore the Chen line.

sentences.zh: 師次芹站，遂造浮橋于昌江以濟。

translations.literal: The army halted at Qin Station and built a pontoon bridge on the Chang River to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at Qin Station and built a pontoon bridge on the Chang River.

sentences.zh: 前鋒抵富良江北嘉林縣，而輔由芹站西取他道至北江府新福縣，諜晟、彬軍亦自雲南至白鶴，乃遣驃騎將軍硃榮往會之。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Jialin County north of the Fu River, while Fu took another route west from Qin Station to Xinfu County in Beijiang Prefecture; intelligence showed Sheng and Bin’s forces also arriving from Yunnan at White Crane; he then sent Cavalry General Zhu Rong to join them.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Jialin north of the Fu River while Fu marched west to Xinfu; Sheng and Bin came from Yunnan to White Crane, and Zhu Rong was sent to unite the columns.

sentences.zh: 時輔等分道進兵，所至皆克。

translations.literal: At that time Fu and the others advanced by separate routes and everywhere prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu’s columns advanced on several routes and carried every position.

sentences.zh: 賊乃緣江樹柵，增築土城於多邦隘，城柵連九百餘里，大發江北民二百余萬守之。

translations.literal: The rebels then lined the river with palisades and built earthen walls at Duobang Pass; ramparts and stockades stretched nine hundred li; more than two million civilians north of the river were mobilized to defend them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified the river with palisades and earthen walls at Duobang Pass for nine hundred li, drafting over two million northern civilians to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 諸江海口皆下木樁，所居東都，嚴守備，水陸兵號七百萬，欲持久以老官軍。

translations.literal: At every river mouth they drove wooden stakes; their capital Dongdu was heavily guarded; land and naval forces were claimed to number seven million, intending to wear down the imperial army by attrition.
translations.idiomatic: They drove stakes at every estuary, fortified Dongdu, and claimed seven million troops by land and sea to exhaust the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 輔等乃移營三帶州個招市江口，造戰艦。

translations.literal: Fu and the others then moved camp to Gezhao Market at the mouth of Sandai Prefecture and built warships.
translations.idiomatic: Fu shifted camp to Gezhao Market and built a fleet.

sentences.zh: 帝慮賊緩師以待瘴癘，敕輔等必以明年春滅賊。

translations.literal: The Emperor, fearing the rebels would delay until miasma season, ordered Fu and the others to destroy the enemy by the following spring at the latest.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing delay until plague season, the Emperor ordered the rebels crushed by the next spring.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晟次洮江北岸，與多邦城對壘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Sheng encamped on the north bank of the Tao River, facing Duobang city across the stream.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Sheng camped north of the Tao River opposite Duobang.

sentences.zh: 輔遣旭攻洮江州，造浮橋濟師，遂俱抵城下，攻拔之。

translations.literal: Fu sent Xu to attack Taojiang Prefecture, built a pontoon bridge to ferry troops, and then all reached below the walls and stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu sent Xu against Taojiang, bridged the river, and stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 賊所恃惟此城，既破，膽裂。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on this city alone; once it fell, their courage broke.
translations.idiomatic: This was their chief stronghold; once it fell, their courage collapsed.

sentences.zh: 大軍循富良江南下，遂搗東都。

translations.literal: The great army followed the Fu River south and struck Dongdu.
translations.idiomatic: The main force marched down the Fu River and assaulted Dongdu.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城走，大軍入據之，薄西都。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned the city and fled; the great army occupied it and pressed Xidu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled; the army occupied Dongdu and pressed Xidu.

sentences.zh: 賊大燒宮室，駕舟入海。

translations.literal: The rebels burned the palaces and took boats to sea.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the palaces and fled by sea.

sentences.zh: 郡縣相繼納款，抗拒者輒擊破之。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties submitted in succession; those who resisted were promptly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Districts submitted one after another; resisters were crushed.

sentences.zh: 士民上書陳黎氏罪惡，日以百數。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners submitted memorials denouncing the crimes of the Le house by the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: Each day hundreds of locals memorialized the Le clan’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 五年正月大破季犛于木丸江，宣詔訪求陳氏子孫。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the army routed Qui Li at Muyuan River and proclaimed an edict seeking Chen descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year’s first month Qui Li was routed at Muyuan River and an edict sought Chen heirs.

sentences.zh: 於是耆老千一百二十餘人詣軍門，言：「陳氏為黎賊殺盡，無可繼者。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than eleven hundred elders came to headquarters, saying: “The Chen house was slaughtered to the last by the Le bandits; none remain to succeed.”
translations.idiomatic: More than eleven hundred elders came to camp saying the Chen line had been exterminated by the Le rebels.

sentences.zh: 安南本中國地，乞仍入職方，同內郡。

translations.literal: “Annan was originally Chinese territory; we beg to be restored to the inner commanderies.”
translations.idiomatic: “Annan was always Chinese land; we beg to return to direct administration.”

sentences.zh: 」輔等以聞。

translations.literal: Fu and the others reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reported their petition.

sentences.zh: 尋大破賊于富良江，季犛父子以數舟遁去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the army again routed the rebels at the Fu River; Qui Li father and son fled in a few boats.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels were routed again at the Fu River; Qui Li and his son escaped in a few boats.

sentences.zh: 諸軍水陸並追，次茶籠縣，知季犛走乂安，遂循舉厥江，追至日南州奇羅海口，命柳升出海追之。

translations.literal: Land and naval forces pursued together; halting at Chalong County, learning Qui Li had fled to Yian, they followed the Jujue River to the Qiluo estuary at Rinan Prefecture and ordered Liu Sheng to pursue by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers learned Qui Li had fled to Yian, followed the Jujue River to Qiluo estuary, and sent Liu Sheng after him by sea.

sentences.zh: 賊數敗，不能軍。

translations.literal: The rebels, repeatedly defeated, could no longer maintain an army.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly beaten, the rebels could no longer hold an army.

sentences.zh: 五月獲季犛及偽太子于高望山，安南盡平。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Qui Li and the false crown prince were captured at Gaowang Mountain; Annan was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qui Li and the false crown prince were taken at Gaowang Mountain; Annan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 群臣請如耆老言，設郡縣。

translations.literal: The ministers requested, as the elders had urged, that prefectures and counties be established.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to establish prefectures and counties as the elders had requested.

sentences.zh: 六月朔，詔告天下，改安南為交阯，設三司：以都督僉事呂毅掌都司事，黃中副之，前工部侍郎張顯宗、福建布政司左參政王平為左、右布政使，前河南按察使阮友彰為按察使，裴伯耆授右參議，又命尚書黃福兼掌布、按二司事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month an edict announced to the realm that Annan was renamed Jiaozhi and three commissions were established: Military Commissioner Lü Yi to manage the regional military commission with Huang Zhong as deputy; former Vice Minister Zhang Xianzong and Fujian Left Administrative Commissioner Wang Ping as left and right provincial commissioners; former Henan Surveillance Commissioner Ruan Youzhang as surveillance commissioner; Pei Bozhe appointed right administrative assistant; Minister Huang Fu was also ordered to oversee both civil commissions.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the sixth month the court announced Annan renamed Jiaozhi with three commissions: Lü Yi military, Zhang Xianzong and Wang Ping civil, Ruan Youzhang surveillance; Pei Bozhe right assistant; Huang Fu overseeing both civil offices.

sentences.zh: 設交州、北江、諒江、三江、建平、新安、建昌、奉化、清化、鎮蠻、諒山、新平、演州、乂安、順化十五府，分轄三十六州，一百八十一縣。

translations.literal: Fifteen prefectures were established—Jiaozhou, Beijiang, Liangjiang, Sanjiang, Jianping, Xin’an, Jianchang, Fenghua, Qinghua, Zhenman, Liangshan, Xinping, Yanzhou, Yian, and Shunhua—governing thirty-six zhou and 181 counties.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen prefectures were set up governing thirty-six zhou and 181 counties.

sentences.zh: 又設太原、宣化、嘉興、歸化、廣威五州，直隸布政司，分轄二十九縣。

translations.literal: Five additional zhou—Taiyuan, Xuanhua, Jiaxing, Guihua, and Guangwei—were placed directly under the provincial commission, governing twenty-nine counties.
translations.idiomatic: Five zhou were placed directly under the provincial commission with twenty-nine counties.

sentences.zh: 其他要害，咸設衛所控制之。

translations.literal: At other strategic points guard posts and battalions were established to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Strategic points were garrisoned with guards and battalions.

sentences.zh: 乃敕有司，陳氏諸王被弑者鹹予贈諡，建祠治塚，各置灑掃二十戶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that murdered Chen princes be granted posthumous titles, temples built, tombs tended, and twenty households assigned for sweeping each.
translations.idiomatic: Murdered Chen princes received posthumous titles, temples, tombs, and twenty sweeping households each.

sentences.zh: 宗族被害者贈官，軍民死亡暴露者瘞埋之。

translations.literal: Clansmen who had been killed were granted posthumous offices; exposed corpses of soldiers and civilians were buried.
translations.idiomatic: Slain clansmen received posthumous ranks; exposed dead were buried.

sentences.zh: 居官者仍其舊，與新除者參治。

translations.literal: Those in office kept their posts and served together with newly appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Incumbent officials remained and served with new appointees.

sentences.zh: 黎氏苛政一切蠲除，遭刑者悉放免。

translations.literal: All harsh Le policies were abolished and those under sentence were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Le exactions were abolished and prisoners freed.

sentences.zh: 禮待高年碩德。

translations.literal: The aged and virtuous were honored with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The aged and worthy were honored.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨無告者設養濟院。

translations.literal: For widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute poorhouses were established.
translations.idiomatic: Poorhouses were set up for widows, orphans, and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 懷才抱德之彥敦遣赴京。

translations.literal: Men of talent and integrity were respectfully sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men were escorted to court.

sentences.zh: 又詔訪求山林隱逸、明經博學、賢良方正、孝弟力田、聰明正直、廉能幹濟、練達吏事、精通書算、明習兵法及容貌魁岸、詔言便利、膂力勇敢、陰陽術數、醫藥方脈諸人，悉以禮敦致，送京錄用。

translations.literal: An edict also sought recluses, classicists, the worthy and upright, filial sons, the intelligent and upright, the incorrupt and capable, experienced clerks, masters of calculation, experts in military law, men of imposing stature, those skilled in profitable counsel, the strong and brave, masters of yin-yang and numerology, and physicians—all to be respectfully summoned and sent to the capital for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts sought recluses, scholars, filial sons, the capable, clerks, mathematicians, strategists, physicians, and more—all to be summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 於是張輔等先後奏舉九千餘人。

translations.literal: Fu and others memorialized recommending more than nine thousand persons in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and others recommended over nine thousand men.

sentences.zh: 九月，季犛、蒼父子俘至闕下，與偽將相胡杜等悉屬吏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Qui Li and his son Cang were brought captive to court, together with the false chancellor Hu Du and others, all handed to the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Qui Li and Cang reached the capital in bonds with Hu Du and other false officials.

sentences.zh: 赦蒼弟衛國大王澄、子芮，所司給衣食。

translations.literal: Cang’s younger brother, the Defender King of Weiguo, Cheng, and his son Rui were pardoned and given food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cang’s brother Cheng and son Rui were pardoned and provided for.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，輔等振旅還京，上交阯地圖，東西一千七百六十里，南北二千八百里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year Fu and others returned victorious to the capital and presented the Jiaozhi map: 1,760 li east to west and 2,800 li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year’s sixth month Fu returned with the map: 1,760 li by 2,800 li.

sentences.zh: 安撫人民三百一十二萬有奇，獲蠻人二百八萬七千五百有奇，象、馬、牛二十三萬五千九百有奇，米粟一千三百六十萬石，船八千六百七十餘艘，軍器二百五十三萬九千八百。

translations.literal: The people pacified numbered more than 3,120,000; barbarians captured 2,875,000 odd; elephants, horses, and cattle 235,900 odd; grain 13,600,000 piculs; ships 8,670 odd; weapons 2,539,800.
translations.idiomatic: They reported 3.12 million people pacified, 2.875 million barbarians captured, vast herds, grain, ships, and arms.

sentences.zh: 於是大行封賞，輔進英國公，晟黔國公，餘敘賚有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon great enfeoffments and rewards were granted: Fu advanced to Duke of Ying, Sheng to Duke of Qian, and the rest received rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fu became Duke of Ying, Sheng Duke of Qian, and others were rewarded by rank.

sentences.zh: 時中朝所置吏，務以寬厚輯新造，而蠻人自以非類，數相驚恐。

translations.literal: At that time officials appointed by the central court aimed to bind the newly conquered territory with leniency, yet the natives, feeling themselves a different people, were repeatedly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Central appointees sought leniency, yet locals, feeling alien, were often terrified.

sentences.zh: 陳氏故官簡定者，先降，將遣詣京師，偕其党陳希葛逃去，與化州偽官鄧悉、阮帥等謀亂。

translations.literal: A former Chen official named Jian Ding, who had surrendered first and was to be sent to the capital, fled with his follower Chen Xige and joined the false officials of Huazhou, Deng Xi and Ruan Shuai, to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen defector Jian Ding was to be sent to court but fled with Chen Xige and joined Deng Xi and Ruan Shuai of Huazhou to rebel.

sentences.zh: 定乃僭大號，紀元興慶，國曰大越。

translations.literal: Ding then usurped a great title, adopted the reign era Xingqing, and styled his state Great Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ding proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yue with the era Xingqing.

sentences.zh: 出沒乂安、化州山中，伺大軍還，即出攻盤灘咸子關，扼三江府往來孔道，寇交州近境。

translations.literal: He ranged the mountains of Yian and Huazhou, waiting until the main army withdrew to attack Pan Beach at Xianzi Pass, block the route through Sanjiang Prefecture, and raid the borders of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He raided from the mountains, seized Xianzi Pass, blocked Sanjiang, and harried Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 慈廉、威蠻、上洪、天堂、應平、石室諸州縣皆向應，守將屢出討，皆無功。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Cilian, Weiman, Shanghong, Tiantang, Yingping, and Shishi all responded; defending generals repeatedly campaigned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Several prefectures joined him and Ming garrisons failed to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命沐晟為征夷將軍，統雲南、貴州、四川軍四萬人，由雲南征討。

translations.literal: On report, Mu Sheng was ordered as General Who Pacifies the Yi to lead forty thousand troops from Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Sheng was ordered to lead forty thousand troops from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 而遣使齎敕招降者予世官。

translations.literal: Envoys carrying edicts offering hereditary offices to those who submitted were also sent.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys offered hereditary rank to defectors.

sentences.zh: 賊不應，晟與戰生厥江，大敗，呂毅及參贊尚書劉俊死之。

translations.literal: The rebels did not respond; Sheng fought them at Shengjue River, suffered a great defeat, and Lü Yi and Minister Liu Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels refused; Sheng was crushed at Shengjue River and Lü Yi and Liu Jun were killed.

sentences.zh: 七年，敗書聞，益發南畿、浙江、江西、福建、湖廣、廣東、廣西軍四萬七千人，從英國公輔征之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when news of defeat arrived, still more troops were levied—forty-seven thousand from the southern provinces—and Zhang Fu again led the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year forty-seven thousand more troops were levied and Zhang Fu marched again.

sentences.zh: 輔以賊負江海，不利陸師，乃駐北江仙遊，大造戰艦，而撫諸遭寇逋播者，遂連破慈廉、廣威諸營柵。

translations.literal: Fu judged that the rebels relied on rivers and coasts and that land forces were ill suited; he encamped at Xianyou in Beijiang, built many warships, pacified displaced people, and successively broke the stockades of Cilian and Guangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Fu camped at Xianyou, built a fleet, pacified refugees, and broke rebel stockades.

sentences.zh: 偵其党鄧景異扼南策州盧渡江太平橋，乃進軍咸子關。

translations.literal: Learning that Deng Jingyi held Taiping Bridge on the Lu River in Nance Prefecture, he advanced on Xianzi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Deng Jingyi held Taiping Bridge, he advanced on Xianzi Pass.

sentences.zh: 偽金吾將軍阮世每眾二萬，對岸立寨柵，列船六百餘艘，樹樁東南以扞蔽。

translations.literal: The false Golden Crow General Ruan Shimei had twenty thousand men on the opposite bank with stockades and more than six hundred boats, with stakes to the southeast for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Shimei held twenty thousand men, six hundred boats, and stake barriers.

sentences.zh: 時八月，西北風急，輔督陳旭、硃廣、俞讓、方政等舟齊進，砲矢飆發，斬首三千級，生擒偽監門將軍潘低等二百餘人，獲船四百餘艘。

translations.literal: It was the eighth month and the northwest wind blew hard; Fu directed Chen Xu, Zhu Guang, Yu Rang, Fang Zheng, and others in a fleet advance; cannon and arrows flew; three thousand heads were taken, more than two hundred including the false Gate Keeper General Pan Di were captured alive, and more than four hundred boats were seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a northwest gale aided Fu’s fleet; three thousand were slain and four hundred boats taken.

sentences.zh: 遂進擊景異，景異先走，乃定交州、北江、諒江、新安、建昌、鎮蠻諸府。

translations.literal: They then attacked Jingyi, who fled first, and secured Jiaozhou, Beijiang, Liangjiang, Xin’an, Jianchang, and Zhenman prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi fled; Jiaozhou and other prefectures were secured.

sentences.zh: 追破景異太平海口，獲其党范必栗。

translations.literal: They routed Jingyi at Taiping estuary and captured his follower Fan Bili.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi was routed at Taiping estuary and Fan Bili captured.

sentences.zh: 時阮帥等推簡定為太上皇，別立陳季擴為帝，紀元重光。

translations.literal: At that time Ruan Shuai and others made Jian Ding Retired Emperor and set up Chen Jikuo as emperor with the era Chongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Shuai made Ding Retired Emperor and set up Chen Jikuo with the era Chongguang.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使自稱前安南王孫，求封爵。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys claiming to be descendants of the former Annan king and requesting enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys claiming Chen descent and begging investiture.

sentences.zh: 輔叱斬之，由黃江、阿江、大安海口至福成江，轉入神投海口，盡去賊所樹樁柵。

translations.literal: Fu rebuked and executed them, then advanced from the Huang, A, and Da’an estuaries to Fucheng River and into Shentou estuary, removing all rebel stakes and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Fu executed the envoys and cleared stakes from the estuaries.

sentences.zh: 十餘日抵清化，水陸畢會。

translations.literal: After more than ten days they reached Qinghua and united land and naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days they reached Qinghua and united.

sentences.zh: 定已奔演州，季擴走乂安，帥、景異等亦散亡。

translations.literal: Ding had fled to Yanzhou, Jikuo to Yian, and Shuai, Jingyi, and others were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Ding fled to Yanzhou, Jikuo to Yian, and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 於是駐軍，捕餘黨。

translations.literal: The army then encamped and hunted down remnant bands.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped and hunted remnants.

sentences.zh: 定走美良縣吉利柵，輔等窮追及之。

translations.literal: Ding fled to Jili stockade in Meiliang County; Fu and others pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Ding fled to Jili stockade and Fu pursued relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 定走入山，大索不得，遂圍之，並其偽將相陳希葛、阮汝勵、阮晏等俱就擒。

translations.literal: Ding entered the mountains and could not be found despite a thorough search; they besieged the area and captured the false ministers Chen Xige, Ruan Ruli, Ruan Yan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Ding hid in the mountains; the siege captured Chen Xige, Ruan Ruli, Ruan Yan, and others.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊党阮師檜僭王，與偽金吾上將軍杜元措等據東潮州安老縣之宜陽社，眾二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier the rebel Ruan Shiguan had usurped the kingship with Du Yuancuo and others at Yiyang commune in Anlao County, Dongchao Prefecture, with more than twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ruan Shiguan had held Yiyang with over twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，輔進擊之，斬首四千五百餘級，擒其党范支、陳原卿、阮人柱等二千餘人，悉斬之，築京觀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Fu attacked, beheading more than four thousand five hundred and capturing Fan Zhi, Chen Yuanqing, Ruan Renzhu, and more than two thousand others—all were executed and a victory mound was raised.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year’s first month Fu slew four thousand five hundred and executed two thousand captives, raising a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 輔將班師，言：「季擴及党阮帥、胡具、鄧景異等尚在演州、晙安，逼清化。

translations.literal: As Fu was about to withdraw he said: “Jikuo and his followers Ruan Shuai, Hu Ju, and Deng Jingyi remain in Yanzhou and Jun’an, pressing Qinghua.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu reported Jikuo and allies still threatened Qinghua.

sentences.zh: 而鄧熔塞神投福成江口，據清化要路，出沒乂安諸處。

translations.literal: “Deng Rong blocks the Fucheng estuary at Shentou and holds the vital route to Qinghua, raiding Yian and elsewhere.”
translations.idiomatic: “Deng Rong blocks Shentou and raids Yian.”

sentences.zh: 若諸軍盡還，恐沐晟兵少不敵。

translations.literal: “If all armies withdraw, I fear Sheng’s force will be too few to resist.”
translations.idiomatic: “If all withdraw, Sheng cannot hold.”

sentences.zh: 請留都督江浩，都指揮俞讓、花英、師祐等軍，佐晟守禦。

translations.literal: “I beg to leave Generals Jiang Hao, Yu Rang, Hua Ying, and Shi You to assist Sheng in defense.”
translations.idiomatic: “Leave Jiang Hao, Yu Rang, Hua Ying, and Shi You with Sheng.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 五月，晟追季擴至虞江，賊棄柵遁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Sheng pursued Jikuo to Yujiang; the rebels abandoned their stockades and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Sheng pursued Jikuo to Yujiang and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 追至古靈縣及會潮、靈長海口，斬首三千餘級，獲偽將軍黎弄。

translations.literal: The pursuit reached Guling County and the estuaries of Huichao and Lingchang; more than three thousand heads were taken and the false general Li Nong captured.
translations.idiomatic: At Guling and the estuaries three thousand were slain and Li Nong captured.

sentences.zh: 季擴大蹙，奉表乞降。

translations.literal: Jikuo, hard pressed, submitted a memorial begging surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Jikuo begged surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝心知其詐，姑許之，詔授交阯布政使，阮帥、胡具、鄧景異、鄧熔並都指揮，陳原樽右參政，潘季祐按察副使。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it was deceitful but for the moment consented, ordering Jikuo made provincial commissioner of Jiaozhi, with Ruan Shuai, Hu Ju, Deng Jingyi, and Deng Rong all regional commanders, Chen Yuanzun right assistant, and Pan Jiyou surveillance vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected deceit but temporarily appointed Jikuo and his chiefs.

sentences.zh: 詔既下，念賊無悛心，九年復命輔督軍二萬四千，合晟軍討之。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, reflecting that the rebels would not repent, in the ninth year he again ordered Fu to command twenty-four thousand troops combined with Sheng’s army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Fu was again ordered with twenty-four thousand men to join Sheng.

sentences.zh: 賊據月常江，樹樁四十餘丈，兩崖置柵二三里，列船三百餘艘，設伏山右。

translations.literal: The rebels held the Yuechang River with stakes forty zhang high; stockades two or three li on both banks; more than three hundred boats; ambushes on the right mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified Yuechang River with forty-zhang stakes, stockades, three hundred boats, and ambushes.

sentences.zh: 秋，輔、晟等水陸並進，阮帥、胡具、鄧景異、鄧钅容等來拒。

translations.literal: In autumn Fu and Sheng advanced by land and water; Ruan Shuai, Hu Ju, Deng Jingyi, and Deng Rong came to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Fu advanced; Shuai and others resisted.

sentences.zh: 輔令硃廣等連艦拔樁以進，自率方政等以步隊剿其伏兵，水陸夾攻。

translations.literal: Fu ordered Zhu Guang and others to link ships and pull out the stakes; he himself led Fang Zheng and infantry to destroy the ambush; land and water attacked together.
translations.idiomatic: Fu’s fleet pulled the stakes while infantry cleared ambushes.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，帥等皆散走。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly defeated and Shuai and the others scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and scattered.

sentences.zh: 生擒偽將軍鄧宗稷、黎德彝、阮忠、阮軒等，獲船百二十艘。

translations.literal: The false generals Deng Zongji, Li Deyi, Ruan Zhong, and Ruan Xuan were captured alive, and one hundred twenty boats were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zongji, Li Deyi, Ruan Zhong, and Ruan Xuan were captured with 120 boats.

sentences.zh: 輔乃督水軍剿季擴，聞石室、福安諸州縣偽龍虎將軍黎蕊等斷銳江浮橋阻生厥江交州後衛道路，遂往征之。

translations.literal: Fu then directed the navy against Jikuo; hearing that the false Dragon-Tiger General Li Rui and others at Shishi and Fu’an had cut the Rui River pontoon and blocked the route behind Jiaozhou, he went to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu turned to Li Rui, who had cut the Rui River bridge behind Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 蕊及範慷來拒，蕊中矢死。

translations.literal: Rui and Fan Kang came to resist; Rui was struck by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Fan Kang resisted; Rui died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 斬偽將軍阮陀，獲偽將軍楊汝梅、防禦使馮翕，斬首千五百級，追殺餘賊殆盡。

translations.literal: The false general Ruan Tuo was beheaded; the false generals Yang Rumei and Defender Feng Xi were captured; fifteen hundred heads were taken and the remaining rebels were nearly all slain.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tuo was beheaded, Yang Rumei and Feng Xi captured, and fifteen hundred slain.

sentences.zh: 慷及杜個旦、鄧明、阮思瑊等亦就擒。

translations.literal: Kang and Du Gedan, Deng Ming, Ruan Sizhen, and others were also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, Du Gedan, Deng Ming, and Ruan Sizhen were captured.

sentences.zh: 十年，輔督方政等擊賊舟於神投海，大敗之，擒偽將軍陳磊、鄧汝戲等。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Fu directed Fang Zheng and others to attack rebel boats at Shentou Sea, routing them and capturing the false general Chen Lei and Deng Ruxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Fu routed rebel boats at Shentou Sea and captured Chen Lei and Deng Ruxi.

sentences.zh: 阮帥等遠遁，追之不及。

translations.literal: Ruan Shuai and others fled far away and could not be overtaken.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Shuai fled beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 輔軍至乂安土黃，偽少保潘季祐等請降，率偽官十七人上謁。

translations.literal: Fu’s army reached Tu Huang in Yian; the false Junior Guardian Pan Jiyou and others begged surrender and led seventeen false officials to audience.
translations.idiomatic: At Tu Huang in Yian, Pan Jiyou and seventeen officials surrendered.

sentences.zh: 輔承制授季祐按察副使，署乂安府事。

translations.literal: Fu, acting on imperial authority, appointed Jiyou surveillance vice commissioner and acting prefect of Yian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu appointed Jiyou surveillance vice commissioner over Yian.

sentences.zh: 於是偽將軍、觀察、安撫、招討諸使陳敏、阮士勤、陳全勖、陳全敏等相繼降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the false generals, observers, pacifiers, and recruitment commissioners Chen Min, Ruan Shiqin, Chen Quanxun, Chen Quanmin, and others surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chen Min, Ruan Shiqin, Chen Quanxun, Chen Quanmin, and others surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 明年，輔及晟合軍至順州。

translations.literal: The next year, Fu and Sheng united their armies and reached Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Fu and Mu Sheng joined forces and advanced to Shun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 阮帥等設伏愛子江，而據昆傳山險，列象陣迎敵。

translations.literal: Ruan Shuai and others set an ambush at the Aizi River, while occupying the perilous heights of Kunzhuan Mountain and deploying an elephant formation to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Shuai laid an ambush on the Aizi River, held the heights of Kunzhuan Mountain, and deployed war elephants against the Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大破之，生擒偽將軍潘徑、阮徐等五十六人，追至愛母江。

translations.literal: The armies routed them utterly, capturing alive the false generals Pan Jing and Ruan Xu and fifty-six others, and pursued to the Aimou River.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming armies crushed the rebels, took fifty-six prisoners including the false generals Pan Jing and Ruan Xu, and pursued them to the Aimou River.

sentences.zh: 賊潰散，鄧钅容弟偽侯鐵及將軍潘魯、潘勤等盡降。

translations.literal: The rebels scattered in defeat; Deng Rong's younger brother, the false marquis Tie, and the generals Pan Lu and Pan Qin all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled; Tie, the false marquis and younger brother of Deng Rong, along with Pan Lu, Pan Qin, and others, all submitted.

sentences.zh: 明年春，進軍政和。

translations.literal: The next spring they advanced on Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the army marched on Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 賊帥胡同降，言偽大將軍景異率党黎蟾等七百人逃暹蠻昆蒲柵。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Hu Tong surrendered, reporting that the false grand general Jing Yi had led a faction including Li Chan and seven hundred men in flight to the Kunpu stockade among the Xian tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Hu Tong surrendered and reported that the false grand general Jing Yi had fled with Li Chan and seven hundred followers to the Kunpu stockade among the Xian tribes.

sentences.zh: 遂進羅蒙江，舍騎步行，比至，賊已遁。

translations.literal: They then advanced to the Luomeng River, dismounted and continued on foot; by the time they arrived, the rebels had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed on to the Luomeng River, left their horses and continued on foot—but the rebels were already gone.

sentences.zh: 追至叱蒲捺柵，又遁。

translations.literal: They pursued to the Chipuna stockade, but the rebels fled again.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached the Chipuna stockade, only for the rebels to escape once more.

sentences.zh: 昏夜行二十餘里，聞更鼓聲，輔率政等銜枚疾趨，黎明抵叱蒲幹柵，江北賊猶寨南岸。

translations.literal: Traveling more than twenty li through the dark of night, they heard the sound of watch-drums; Fu led Zheng and others with gags in their mouths in a swift advance, and at dawn reached the Chipugan stockade—the rebels on the north bank still encamped on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: After marching twenty-odd li through the night and hearing watch-drums, Zhang Fu led Fang Zheng and others in a silent forced march; at dawn they reached the Chipugan stockade, where rebels north of the river still held camps on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 官軍渡江圍之，矢中景異脅，擒之。

translations.literal: The government troops crossed the river and surrounded them; an arrow struck Jing Yi in the side and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops crossed the river and besieged the camp; Jing Yi was struck in the side by an arrow and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 鎔及弟鈗亡走，追擒之，盡獲其眾。

translations.literal: Rong and his younger brother Yun fled; they were pursued and captured, and all their followers were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Rong and his brother Yun tried to flee but were captured along with all their men.

sentences.zh: 別將硃廣追偽大將軍阮帥于暹蠻，大搜暹人關諸山，獲帥及季擴等家屬。

translations.literal: The deputy general Zhu Guang pursued the false grand general Ruan Shuai among the Xian tribes, thoroughly searched the mountains of the Xian Pass, and captured Shuai and the families of Ji Kuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Zhu Guang pursued Ruan Shuai among the Xian tribes, searched the mountains of the Xian Pass, and captured Shuai along with the families of Chen Ji Kuo and others.

sentences.zh: 帥逃南靈州，依土官阮茶匯。

translations.literal: Shuai fled to Nanling Prefecture and sought refuge with the native official Ruan Chahui.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Shuai fled to Nanling Prefecture and took shelter with the native official Ruan Chahui.

sentences.zh: 指揮薛聚追獲帥，斬茶匯。

translations.literal: The commander Xue Ju pursued and captured Shuai and beheaded Chahui.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Xue Ju ran Shuai down and killed Chahui.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧鎔之就執也，季擴逃乂安竹排山。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deng Rong was taken prisoner, Ji Kuo fled to Zhupai Mountain in Yian.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Rong was captured, Chen Ji Kuo had fled to Zhupai Mountain in Yian.

sentences.zh: 輔遣都指揮師祐襲之，走老撾。

translations.literal: Fu sent the regional commander Shi You to raid him; Ji Kuo fled to Laos.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu sent Regional Commander Shi You after him; Chen Ji Kuo fled into Laos.

sentences.zh: 祐踵其後，老撾懼官軍躪其地，請自縛以獻。

translations.literal: You followed on his heels; Laos, fearing that government troops would trample its territory, offered to bind Ji Kuo and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi You pressed the pursuit; fearing a Ming incursion, the Laotians offered to bind Chen Ji Kuo and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 輔檄索之，令祐深入，克三關，抵金陵個，賊黨盡奔，遂獲季擴及其弟偽相國驩國王季揝，他賊盡平。

translations.literal: Fu issued orders demanding him; he had You push deep, took three passes, reached Jinlingge, and the rebel factions all fled; they then captured Ji Kuo and his younger brother, the false chancellor and King of Huan, Ji San, and all other rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu ordered Shi You to push deep into Laos; after taking three passes and reaching Jinlingge, the rebels scattered. Chen Ji Kuo was captured along with his younger brother Ji San, the false chancellor and King of Huan, and the remaining rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，輔、晟等班師入京。

translations.literal: The next February Fu, Sheng, and the others withdrew the army and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following February Zhang Fu and Mu Sheng led the army home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四月復命輔佩征夷將軍印，出鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Fu was again ordered to wear the seal of General Who Expands the Yi and go out to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhang Fu was again invested with the seal of General Who Expands the Yi and sent back to garrison Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 十四年召還。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 明年命豐城侯李彬代鎮。

translations.literal: The next year the Marquis of Fengcheng, Li Bin, was ordered to replace him in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Bin, Marquis of Fengcheng, was appointed to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 交人故好亂。

translations.literal: The people of Jiaozhi have always been prone to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiaozhi had long been restive.

sentences.zh: 中官馬騏以採辦至，大索境內珍寶，人情騷動，桀黠者鼓煽之，大軍甫還，即並起為亂。

translations.literal: The eunuch Ma Qi arrived on a procurement mission and searched the entire region for precious goods; popular sentiment was stirred to unrest, and the crafty and bold incited it; scarcely had the main army returned when rebellions broke out together.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Ma Qi arrived to procure tribute goods and looted the province for treasures, unrest spread; as soon as the main army withdrew, rebels rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 陸那阮貞，順州黎核、潘強與土官同知陳可論、判官阮昭、千戶陳忷、南靈州判官阮擬、左平知縣范伯高、縣丞武萬、百戶陳已律等一時並反。

translations.literal: Ruan Zhen of Lu Na, Li He and Pan Qiang of Shun Prefecture, together with the native official Vice Commissioner Chen Kelun, Vice Magistrate Ruan Zhao, Company Commander Chen Xiong, Vice Magistrate Ruan Ni of Nanling Prefecture, Magistrate Fan Bogao of Zuoping, Assistant Magistrate Wu Wan, Platoon Commander Chen Yilü, and others all rebelled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhen of Lu Na, Li He and Pan Qiang of Shun Prefecture, Chen Kelun, Ruan Zhao, Chen Xiong, Ruan Ni, Fan Bogao, Wu Wan, Chen Yilü, and others all rebelled at once.

sentences.zh: 彬皆遣將討滅之，而反者猶不止。

translations.literal: Bin sent generals to attack and destroy them, but the rebels still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin sent generals to suppress each rising, but rebellion continued unabated.

sentences.zh: 俄樂巡檢黎利、四忙故知縣車綿之子三、乂安知府潘僚、南靈州千戶陳順慶、乂安衛百戶陳直誠，亦乘機作亂。

translations.literal: The Olai district inspector Le Loi, Che San—the son of the former magistrate of Simang, Che Mian—the prefect of Yian Pan Liao, the company commander of Nanling Chen Shunqing, and the platoon commander of the Yian Guard Chen Zhicheng also seized the moment to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi, district inspector of Olai; Che San, son of the former Simang magistrate Che Mian; Pan Liao, prefect of Yian; Chen Shunqing of Nanling; and Chen Zhicheng of the Yian Guard also seized the moment to rebel.

sentences.zh: 其他奸宄，範軟起俄樂，武貢、黃汝曲起偈江，儂文曆起丘溫，陳木果起武定，阮特起快州，吳巨來起善誓，鄭公證、黎侄起同利，陶強起善才，丁宗老起大灣，范玉起安老，皆自署官爵，殺將吏，焚廬舍。

translations.literal: Other villains: Fan Ruan rose in Olai; Wu Gong and Huang Ruqu in Jiejiang; Nong Wenli in Qiuwen; Chen Muguo in Wuding; Ruan Te in Kuaizhou; Wu Julai in Shanshi; Zheng Gongzheng and Li Zhi in Tongli; Tao Qiang in Shancai; Ding Zonglao in Dawan; Fan Yu in Anlao—all appointing themselves to titles, killing commanders and officials, and burning buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels followed: Fan Ruan in Olai, Wu Gong and Huang Ruqu in Jiejiang, Nong Wenli in Qiuwen, Chen Muguo in Wuding, Ruan Te in Kuaizhou, Wu Julai in Shanshi, Zheng Gongzheng and Li Zhi in Tongli, Tao Qiang in Shancai, Ding Zonglao in Dawan, and Fan Yu in Anlao—all proclaiming titles, killing officials, and burning settlements.

sentences.zh: 有楊恭、阮多者，皆自稱王，署其党韋五、譚興邦、阮嘉為太師、平章，與群寇相倚，而潘僚、范玉尤猖獗。

translations.literal: Yang Gong and Ruan Duo each styled themselves king, appointing their followers Wei Wu, Tan Xingbang, and Ruan Jia as grand tutor and grand chancellor; they leaned on the band of rebels, while Pan Liao and Fan Yu were especially rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gong and Ruan Duo each declared themselves king, appointing Wei Wu, Tan Xingbang, and Ruan Jia as grand tutor and grand chancellor; they backed one another, but Pan Liao and Fan Yu were the most violent.

sentences.zh: 僚者，故乂安知府季祐子也，嗣父職，不堪馬騏虐，遂反。

translations.literal: Liao was the son of the former prefect of Yian, Jiyou; he succeeded to his father's post but could not endure Ma Qi's cruelty and so rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Liao was the son of the former Yian prefect Pan Jiyou; he had inherited his father's office but rebelled under the eunuch Ma Qi's oppression.

sentences.zh: 土官指揮路文律、千戶陳苔等從之。

translations.literal: The native official commander Lu Wenlü, company commander Chen Tai, and others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The native official commander Lu Wenlü, company commander Chen Tai, and others joined him.

sentences.zh: 玉為塗山寺僧，自言天降印劍，遂僭稱羅平王，紀元永甯，與范善、吳中、黎行、陶承等為亂，署為相國、司空、大將軍，攻掠城邑。

translations.literal: Yu was a monk at Tushan Temple; claiming that seal and sword had descended from heaven, he usurped the title King of Luoping, reign era Yongning, and with Fan Shan, Wu Zhong, Li Xing, Tao Cheng, and others made rebellion, appointing them chancellor, minister of works, and grand general, and raiding cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yu had been a monk at Tushan Temple; claiming heaven-sent seal and sword, he styled himself King of Luoping with the reign era Yongning, rallied Fan Shan, Wu Zhong, Li Xing, and Tao Cheng, and appointed them chancellor, minister of works, and grand general while raiding towns across the province.

sentences.zh: 彬東西征剿，日不暇給。

translations.literal: Bin campaigned east and west to suppress them, with never a day's respite.
