translations.idiomatic: Li Bin was fighting rebels on every front and could scarcely keep pace.

sentences.zh: 中朝以賊久未平，十八年命榮昌伯陳智為左參將，助之。

translations.literal: Because the rebels had long gone unpacified, in the eighteenth year the court appointed the Earl of Rongchang, Chen Zhi, as left regional vice commander to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court sent Chen Zhi, Earl of Rongchang, as left regional vice commander to assist Li Bin.

sentences.zh: 又降敕責彬曰：「叛寇潘僚、黎利、車三、儂文曆等迄今未獲，兵何時得息，民何時得安。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued rebuking Bin: "The rebel bandits Pan Liao, Le Loi, Che San, Nong Wenli, and others have still not been captured—when will the troops rest, and when will the people know peace?
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Li Bin: "The rebels Pan Liao, Le Loi, Che San, and Nong Wenli remain at large—when will the armies stand down and the people live in peace?

sentences.zh: 宣廣為方略，速奏蕩平。

translations.literal: Proclaim your broad strategy and quickly report their complete extermination."
translations.idiomatic: Lay out your strategy and report when the rebels are utterly destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」彬皇恐，督諸將追剿。

translations.literal: Bin was struck with terror and urged the generals to pursue and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin, terrified, pressed his generals to hunt the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，賊悉破滅，惟黎利不能得。

translations.literal: The next autumn the rebels were all broken and destroyed, except that Le Loi could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn nearly every rebel band was crushed—only Le Loi remained at large.

sentences.zh: 利初仕陳季擴為金吾將軍，後歸正，用為清化府俄樂縣巡檢，邑邑不得志。

translations.literal: Le Loi had first served Chen Ji Kuo as Golden Guard general; later he submitted to the Ming and was appointed district inspector of Olai County in Qinghua Prefecture, but he was dissatisfied and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi had first served Chen Ji Kuo as a Golden Guard general, then submitted to the Ming and was made district inspector of Olai in Qinghua Prefecture—but he remained bitter and discontented.

sentences.zh: 及大軍還，遂反，僭稱平定王，以弟石為相國，與其党段莽、范柳、范晏等放兵肆掠。

translations.literal: When the main army withdrew, he rebelled, usurped the title Pacification King, made his younger brother Shi chancellor, and with his followers Duan Mang, Fan Liu, Fan Yan, and others let their troops loose in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew, he rebelled, styled himself Pacification King, made his brother Shi chancellor, and with Duan Mang, Fan Liu, Fan Yan, and others unleashed his men in plunder.

sentences.zh: 官軍討之，生擒晏等，利遁去。

translations.literal: Government troops attacked them, capturing Yan and others alive; Le Loi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops captured Yan and others, but Le Loi got away.

sentences.zh: 久之，出據可藍柵行劫。

translations.literal: After a long while he emerged to occupy the Kelan stockade and raided.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reappeared at the Kelan stockade and resumed raiding.

sentences.zh: 諸將方政、師祐剿獲其偽將軍阮個立等，利逃匿老撾。

translations.literal: The generals Fang Zheng and Shi You suppressed and captured his false generals Ruan Gelì and others; Le Loi fled and hid in Laos.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zheng and Shi You captured his false generals Ruan Gelì and others, but Le Loi fled into Laos.

sentences.zh: 及政等還，利潛出，殺玉局巡檢。

translations.literal: When Zheng and the others returned, Le Loi slipped out secretly and killed the Yuju district inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fang Zheng withdrew, Le Loi stole out and murdered the Yuju district inspector.

sentences.zh: 已，復出掠磊江，每追擊輒遁去。

translations.literal: Before long he again came out to raid Leijiang; each time pursuit was mounted he would escape.
translations.idiomatic: He soon raided along the Lei River again, always melting away whenever troops gave chase.

sentences.zh: 及群盜盡滅，利益深匿。

translations.literal: When all the other bandits had been destroyed, Le Loi hid all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: As the other rebel bands were wiped out, Le Loi buried himself deeper in hiding.

sentences.zh: 彬奏言：「利竄老撾，老撾請官軍毋入，黨盡發所部兵捕利。

translations.literal: Bin memorialized: "Le Loi has fled into Laos; Laos asks that government troops not enter and promises to deploy all its own forces to capture Le Loi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin reported: "Le Loi has fled to Laos, which asks that Ming troops stay out and promises to hunt him with its own forces.

sentences.zh: 今久不遣，情叵測。

translations.literal: Yet it has long failed to deliver him—the situation is impossible to fathom."
translations.idiomatic: But month after month has passed without his surrender; their intentions are deeply suspect."

sentences.zh: 」帝疑老撾匿賊，令彬送其使臣至京詰問，老撾乃逐利。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected Laos of harboring the rebel and ordered Bin to send its envoy to the capital for interrogation; Laos then drove Le Loi out.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected Laos of sheltering the rebel and had its envoy brought to the capital for questioning; only then did the Laotians expel Le Loi.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，彬卒，詔智代彬。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year Bin died; an edict ordered Chen Zhi to replace Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year Li Bin died, and Chen Zhi was appointed to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，智追利於甯化州車來縣，敗之，利復遠竄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Chen Zhi pursued Le Loi to Chelai County in Ninghua Prefecture, defeated him, and Le Loi again fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Chen Zhi routed Le Loi at Chelai in Ninghua Prefecture, but Le Loi escaped once more.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，智奏利初逃老撾，後被逐歸瑰縣。

translations.literal: The next autumn Chen Zhi reported that Le Loi had first fled to Laos, then was expelled and returned to Gui County.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Chen Zhi reported that Le Loi had first fled to Laos, been expelled, and returned to Gui County.

sentences.zh: 官軍進擊，其頭目范仰等已率男婦千六百人降，利雖求撫，願以所部來歸，而止俄樂不出，造國器未已，必當進兵。

translations.literal: Government troops advanced to attack; his chieftains Fan Yang and others had already led sixteen hundred men and women in surrender; although Le Loi sought pacification and wished to bring his followers in submission, he would not come out of Olai, and continued to manufacture regalia; an advance must be made.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed the attack; chieftains such as Fan Yang had already surrendered with sixteen hundred followers. Le Loi asked for amnesty and promised to submit, yet he would not leave Olai and kept forging royal regalia—the army had to advance.

sentences.zh: 奏至，會仁宗以踐阼大赦天下，因敕智善撫之，而利已寇茶籠州，敗方政軍，殺指揮伍雲。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it happened that Renzong, on ascending the throne, had proclaimed a general amnesty; accordingly he ordered Chen Zhi to treat Le Loi with kindness—but Le Loi had already raided Chalong Prefecture, defeated Fang Zheng's army, and killed the commander Wu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial arrived just as Renzong proclaimed a general amnesty on his accession; the Emperor ordered Chen Zhi to offer Le Loi lenient terms—but Le Loi had already raided Chalong, routed Fang Zheng, and killed Commander Wu Yun.

sentences.zh: 利未叛時，與鎮守中官山壽善。

translations.literal: Before Le Loi rebelled, he was on good terms with the garrison eunuch Shan Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Before his rebellion Le Loi had been friendly with the garrison eunuch Shan Shou.

sentences.zh: 至是壽還朝，力言利與己相信，今往諭之，必來歸。

translations.literal: At this time Shou returned to court and insisted that Le Loi trusted him; if he went now to instruct Le Loi, Le Loi would surely come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Shou now returned to court and assured the Emperor that Le Loi trusted him and would submit if he went to reason with him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此賊狡詐，若為所紿，則其勢益熾，不易制也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This bandit is cunning and deceitful; if deceived by him, his power will only grow stronger and he will be harder to control."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "This rebel is cunning; if we are taken in, his power will only grow and he will be harder to subdue."

sentences.zh: 」壽叩頭言：「如臣往諭，而利不來，臣當萬死。

translations.literal: Shou kowtowed and said: "If I go to instruct him and Le Loi does not come, I deserve ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Shan Shou kowtowed and said: "If I go and Le Loi does not submit, I deserve death."

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之，遣壽齎敕授利清化知府，慰諭甚至。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded assent and sent Shou bearing an edict appointing Le Loi prefect of Qinghua, with exceedingly generous words of reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented and sent Shan Shou with an edict appointing Le Loi prefect of Qinghua, offering lavish reassurances.

sentences.zh: 敕甫降，利已寇清化，殺都指揮陳忠。

translations.literal: Hardly had the edict been issued when Le Loi was already raiding Qinghua and had killed the regional commander Chen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict even arrived, Le Loi was raiding Qinghua and had killed Regional Commander Chen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 利得敕，無降意，即借撫愚守臣，佯言俟秋涼赴官，而寇掠不已。

translations.literal: Le Loi received the edict but had no intention of submitting; he immediately exploited the offer of pacification to deceive the garrison officials, pretending he would take office when the autumn cool came, while raiding without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi showed no sign of surrender; he used the offer of amnesty to string the garrison along, claiming he would take office once the weather cooled, while continuing to raid.

sentences.zh: 時洪熙改元，鑄將軍印分頒邊將，智得征夷副將軍印，又命安平伯李甯往佐之。

translations.literal: At that time the Hongxi reign was proclaimed; general's seals were cast and distributed to frontier commanders; Chen Zhi received the seal of Deputy General Who Expands the Yi, and the Earl of Anping, Li Ning, was also ordered to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new Hongxi reign, fresh general's seals were cast for frontier commanders; Chen Zhi received the seal of Deputy General Who Expands the Yi, and Li Ning, Earl of Anping, was sent to assist him.

sentences.zh: 智素無將略，憚賊，因借撫以愚中朝，且與方政迕，遂頓兵不進。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi had never had military talent; he feared the rebels, and so exploited the talk of pacification to deceive the court; moreover he was at odds with Fang Zheng, and thus halted his army and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi was no soldier; afraid of the rebels, he played along with the pacification talk to mislead the court, clashed with Fang Zheng, and refused to move his troops.

sentences.zh: 賊益無所忌，再圍茶籠，智等坐視不救。

translations.literal: The rebels grew all the bolder, besieged Chalong again, and Chen Zhi and the others sat by and did not rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, the rebels besieged Chalong again while Chen Zhi and his officers looked on without lifting a hand.

sentences.zh: 閱七月，城中糧盡，巡按御史以聞，奏至而仁宗崩。

translations.literal: After seven months the city's grain was exhausted; the touring censor reported it; the memorial arrived just as Renzong died.
translations.idiomatic: After seven months the city ran out of provisions; the touring censor reported the crisis—but the memorial reached the capital only as Renzong lay dying.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初即位，敕責智及三司官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande's accession, an edict rebuked Chen Zhi and the three commission officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor took the throne, he rebuked Chen Zhi and the provincial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 智等不為意，茶籠遂陷，知州琴彭死之。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi and the others paid no heed; Chalong then fell, and the prefect Qin Peng died in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi ignored the rebuke; Chalong fell, and Prefect Qin Peng died defending it.

sentences.zh: 尚書掌布按二司陳洽言：「利雖乞降，內攜貳，既陷茶籠，復結玉麻土官、老撾酋長與之同惡。

translations.literal: Minister Chen Qia, who oversaw the provincial and surveillance commissions, said: "Although Le Loi begs to surrender, inwardly he is disloyal; having already taken Chalong, he has again allied with the Yuma native official and Laotian chieftains in wicked collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Qia, who oversaw the provincial and surveillance commissions, reported: "Le Loi feigns surrender while plotting treason; having taken Chalong, he has allied with the Yuma native official and Laotian chiefs.

sentences.zh: 始言俟秋涼，今秋已過，復言與參政梁汝笏有怨，乞改授茶籠州，而遣逆党潘僚、路文律等往嘉興、廣威諸州招集徒眾，勢日滋蔓。

translations.literal: He first said he would wait for the autumn cool; now autumn has passed, and he again claims a grievance against Administrative Vice Commissioner Liang Ruhe, begging to be reassigned to Chalong Prefecture, while dispatching his rebel followers Pan Liao, Lu Wenlü, and others to Jiaxing, Guangwei, and other prefectures to gather followers—the momentum grows daily."
translations.idiomatic: He had promised to surrender once the weather cooled; autumn passed and he pleaded a feud with Vice Commissioner Liang Ruhe, asked for Chalong instead, and sent Pan Liao and Lu Wenlü to rally recruits across Jiaxing and Guangwei—the rebellion spread daily."

sentences.zh: 乞命總兵者速行剿滅。

translations.literal: I beg that the commander-in-chief be ordered to move swiftly to suppress and destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the commander-in-chief be ordered to crush them at once."

sentences.zh: 」奏上，為降敕切責，期來春平賊。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict of stern rebuke was issued, fixing the coming spring as the deadline to pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial prompted a stern imperial rebuke, with a deadline of the following spring to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 智始懼，與政薄可留關，敗還，至茶籠又敗。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi at last grew afraid; he and Zheng fought a brief engagement at Keliu Pass, were defeated and withdrew, and were defeated again at Chalong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi at last moved; he and Fang Zheng fought at Keliu Pass, were beaten back, and lost again at Chalong.

sentences.zh: 政勇而寡謀，智懦而多忌，素不相能，而山壽專招撫，擁兵晙安不救，是以屢敗。

translations.literal: Zheng was brave but lacked strategy; Chen Zhi was timid and jealous—they had never gotten along—while Shan Shou monopolized the pacification effort, holding troops at Juan and refusing to rescue; hence repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zheng was brave but rash, Chen Zhi timid and jealous—they had never cooperated—while Shan Shou clung to pacification talk and kept his troops at Juan without aiding them; hence the repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年春，事聞，復降敕切責。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xuande, when word reached the court, another edict of stern rebuke was issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xuande 1, when the news reached court, the Emperor issued another stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 時渠魁未平，而小寇蜂起，美留潘可利助逆，宣化周莊、太原黃庵等結雲南寧遠州紅衣賊大掠。

translations.literal: At that time the chief rebels had not yet been pacified, while lesser bandits swarmed like bees; Mei Liu and Pan Keli aided the rebellion; Zhuang of Xuanhua, Huang An of Taiyuan, and others joined the Red-Clad bandits of Ningyuan Prefecture in Yunnan in great raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The chief rebels were still loose while lesser bands multiplied; Mei Liu and Pan Keli aided the revolt, and Zhuang of Xuanhua and Huang An of Taiyuan joined Yunnan's Red-Clad bandits of Ningyuan in wide-ranging raids.

sentences.zh: 帝敕沐晟剿寧遠，又發西南諸衛軍萬五千、弩手三千赴交阯，且敕老撾不得容叛人。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Mu Sheng to suppress Ningyuan, also mobilized fifteen thousand troops from the southwestern guards and three thousand crossbowmen for Jiaozhi, and further ordered Laos not to harbor rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Mu Sheng to pacify Ningyuan, sent fifteen thousand southwestern troops and three thousand crossbowmen to Jiaozhi, and forbade Laos to shelter rebels.

sentences.zh: 四月，命成山侯王通為征夷將軍，都督馬瑛為參將，往討黎利。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Marquis of Chengshan, Wang Tong, was appointed General Who Expands the Yi, and the commissioner Ma Ying regional vice commander, to campaign against Le Loi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wang Tong, Marquis of Chengshan, was named General Who Expands the Yi, with Ma Ying as vice commander, to march against Le Loi.

sentences.zh: 削陳智、方政職，充為事官。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi and Fang Zheng were stripped of rank and reduced to officers on probation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi and Fang Zheng were demoted to probationary service.

sentences.zh: 通未至，賊犯清化。

translations.literal: Before Tong arrived, the rebels invaded Qinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Tong's arrival the rebels struck Qinghua.

sentences.zh: 政不出戰，都指揮王演擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zheng did not go out to fight; the regional commander Wang Yan struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zheng held back, but Regional Commander Wang Yan drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 詔大赦交阯罪人，黎利、潘僚降亦授職；

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed a general amnesty for criminals in Jiaozhi; if Le Loi and Pan Liao submitted they would also be given office;
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed for Jiaozhi; Le Loi and Pan Liao were promised posts if they surrendered;

sentences.zh: 停採辦金銀、香貨，冀以弭賊，而賊無悛心。

translations.literal: Procurement of gold, silver, and aromatic goods was halted, in hope of quelling the rebels—but the rebels had no thought of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute levies of gold, silver, and aromatics were suspended in hopes of ending the rebellion, but the rebels would not relent.

sentences.zh: 政督諸軍進討，李安及都指揮于瓚、謝鳳、薛聚、硃廣等先奔，政由此敗，俱謫為事官，立功贖罪。

translations.literal: Zheng directed the armies in advance to attack; Li An and the regional commanders Yu Zan, Xie Feng, Xue Ju, and Zhu Guang fled first; Zheng was thereby defeated; all were demoted to officers on probation to redeem their guilt through merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zheng led an advance; Li An and regional commanders Yu Zan, Xie Feng, Xue Ju, and Zhu Guang broke and ran, and Zheng was routed. All were demoted to probationary service to redeem themselves by merit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，智遣都指揮袁亮擊賊黎善於廣威州，欲渡河，土官何加伉言有伏。

translations.literal: Before long Chen Zhi sent the regional commander Yuan Liang to attack the rebel Li Shan at Guangwei Prefecture; about to cross the river, the native official He Jiakang said there was an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Zhi sent Regional Commander Yuan Liang against the rebel Li Shan at Guangwei; as Liang prepared to cross the river, the native official He Jiakang warned of an ambush.

sentences.zh: 亮不從，遣指揮陶森、錢輔等渡河，中伏並死，亮亦被執。

translations.literal: Liang did not listen; he sent the commanders Tao Sen and Qian Fu and others to cross the river; they fell into an ambush and all died; Liang was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Liang ignored the warning; Tao Sen and Qian Fu crossed the river, walked into an ambush, and were killed; Liang himself was taken.

sentences.zh: 善遂分兵三道犯交州，其攻下關者為都督陳濬所敗，攻邊江小門者為李安所敗，善夜走。

translations.literal: Shan then divided his forces into three columns to invade Jiaozhou; those attacking Xiaguan were defeated by the commissioner Chen Jun; those attacking the small gate at Bianjiang were defeated by Li An; Shan fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan then split his force into three columns against Jiaozhou; the column at Xiaguan was beaten by Commissioner Chen Jun, the column at Bianjiang's lesser gate by Li An, and Shan fled by night.

sentences.zh: 通聞之，亦分兵三道出擊。

translations.literal: When Tong heard of it, he too divided his forces into three columns and sallied forth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong likewise divided his army into three columns and counterattacked.

sentences.zh: 馬瑛敗賊清威，至石室與通會，俱至應平寧橋。

translations.literal: Ma Ying defeated the rebels at Qingwei, reached Shishi and joined Tong, and both proceeded to the Yingping Ning Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ying defeated the rebels at Qingwei, joined Wang Tong at Shishi, and both marched to the Yingping Ning Bridge.

sentences.zh: 士卒行泥濘中，遇伏兵，大敗。

translations.literal: The soldiers marched through mud and mire, encountered ambush troops, and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Trudging through mud, the soldiers walked into an ambush and were routed.

sentences.zh: 尚書陳洽死焉，通亦中脅還。

translations.literal: Minister Chen Qia died there; Tong was also struck in the side and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Qia was killed; Wang Tong was wounded in the side and retreated.

sentences.zh: 利在乂安聞之，鼓行至清潭，攻北江，進圍東關。

translations.literal: Le Loi, in Yian, heard of it and drummed his men onward to Qingtan, attacked Beijiang, and advanced to besiege Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi, in Yian, heard the news and marched swiftly to Qingtan, struck Beijiang, and advanced to besiege Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 通素無戰功，以父真死事封。

translations.literal: Tong had never had military merit; he had been enfeoffed because his father Zhen died in service.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong had no record of military achievement; he held his title only because his father Wang Zhen had died in service.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知其庸劣，誤用之。

translations.literal: The court did not know his mediocrity and incompetence and mistakenly employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unaware of his incompetence, had placed him in command by mistake.

sentences.zh: 一戰而敗，心膽皆喪，舉動乖張，不奉朝命，擅割清化以南地予賊，盡撤官吏軍民還東關。

translations.literal: After one battle and defeat, his heart and courage were utterly lost; his conduct became erratic; he disobeyed court orders, on his own authority ceded all territory south of Qinghua to the rebels, and withdrew all officials, troops, and civilians back to Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: One defeat broke his nerve; he defied orders, unilaterally ceded everything south of Qinghua to the rebels, and pulled all officials, soldiers, and civilians back to Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 惟清化知州羅通不從，利移兵攻之不下。

translations.literal: Only the Qinghua prefect Luo Tong refused to obey; Le Loi shifted his forces to attack him but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qinghua Prefect Luo Tong held fast; Le Loi shifted to besiege him but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵萬人圍隘留關，百戶萬琮奮擊，乃退。

translations.literal: The rebels divided ten thousand men to besiege Ailiu Pass; the platoon commander Wan Cong fought fiercely and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent ten thousand men to besiege Ailiu Pass; Platoon Commander Wan Cong fought them off and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝聞通敗，大駭，命安遠侯柳升為總兵官，保定伯梁銘副之，督師赴討，又命沐晟為征南將軍，興安伯徐亨、新甯伯譚忠為左、右副將軍，從雲南進兵，兩軍共七萬餘人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of Tong's defeat he was greatly alarmed; he appointed the Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Sheng, commander-in-chief, with the Earl of Baoding, Liang Ming, as deputy, to lead troops to suppress them; he also appointed Mu Sheng General Who Expands the South, with the Earl of Xing'an, Xu Heng, and the Earl of Xinning, Tan Zhong, as left and right deputy generals, to advance from Yunnan—the two armies totaling more than seventy thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Horrified by Wang Tong's defeat, the Emperor appointed Liu Sheng, Marquis of Anyuan, commander-in-chief with Liang Ming, Earl of Baoding, as deputy, and dispatched Mu Sheng as General Who Expands the South with Xu Heng and Tan Zhong as deputies from Yunnan—more than seventy thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 復敕通固守，俟升。

translations.literal: He also ordered Tong to hold firm and await Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong was ordered to hold his ground until Liu Sheng arrived.

sentences.zh: 二年春，利犯交州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Le Loi invaded Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xuande 2, Le Loi struck Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 通與戰，斬偽太監黎秘及太尉、司徒、司空等官，獲首級萬計。

translations.literal: Tong fought him, beheaded the false grand eunuch Li Mi and officials bearing the titles of grand commandant, minister of education, and minister of works, and took heads numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong met him in battle, killed the false grand eunuch Li Mi along with grand commandant, minister of education, and minister of works, and claimed ten thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 利破膽奔遁，諸將請乘勢追之，通逗留三日。

translations.literal: Le Loi, his courage broken, fled in panic; the generals asked to pursue on the momentum, but Tong lingered three days.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi broke and ran; his officers urged a hot pursuit, but Wang Tong held back for three days.

sentences.zh: 賊知其怯，復立寨濬濠，四出剽掠。

translations.literal: The rebels, knowing his cowardice, again raised stockades and dug moats, and raided in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his timidity, the rebels rebuilt fortifications and sent raiding parties in every direction.

sentences.zh: 三月復發三萬三千人，從柳升、沐晟征討。

translations.literal: In the third month another thirty-three thousand men were mobilized to campaign under Liu Sheng and Mu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month thirty-three thousand more troops were dispatched under Liu Sheng and Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵圍丘溫，都指揮孫聚力拒之。

translations.literal: The rebels divided their forces to besiege Qiuwen; Regional Commander Sun Ju resisted with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split their army to besiege Qiuwen; Regional Commander Sun Ju held them off.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊以昌江為大軍往來要道，發眾八萬餘人來攻，都指揮李任等力拒，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the rebels regarded the Chang River as the main route for the grand army's coming and going, they dispatched more than eighty thousand men to attack; Regional Commander Li Ren and others resisted fiercely and killed very many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels, treating the Chang River as the army's lifeline, had sent more than eighty thousand men against it; Regional Commander Li Ren and his men fought hard and killed great numbers.

sentences.zh: 閱九月，諸將觀望不救，賊懼升大軍至，攻益力。

translations.literal: After nine months the generals watched and did not rescue; the rebels, fearing Liu Sheng's grand army would arrive, pressed the attack all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Nine months passed while the generals looked on without relief; the rebels, dreading Liu Sheng's arrival, redoubled their assault.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，城陷，任死之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer the city fell, and Ren died in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the city fell and Li Ren died defending it.

sentences.zh: 時賊圍交州久，通閉城不敢出，賊益易之，致書請和。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels had long besieged Jiaozhou; Tong closed the city and dared not emerge—the rebels looked on him with growing contempt and sent a letter proposing peace.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long blockaded Jiaozhou; Wang Tong shut the gates and would not come out, and they grew bolder, sending a letter to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 通欲許之，集眾議，按察使楊時習曰：「奉命討賊，與之和，而擅退師，何以逃罪！

translations.literal: Tong wished to accept; he gathered everyone for deliberation. Surveillance Commissioner Yang Shixi said: "We were ordered to suppress the rebels—if we make peace with them and withdraw the army on our own authority, how can we escape punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong wanted to agree and called a council. Surveillance Commissioner Yang Shixi said, "We were sent to crush the rebels. To make peace and withdraw on our own—how do we answer for that?

sentences.zh: 」通怒，厲聲叱之，眾不敢言，遂以利書聞。

translations.literal: " Tong flew into a rage and shouted him down; no one dared speak, and he reported Le Loi's letter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Tong erupted and shouted him down; no one else spoke, and he forwarded Le Loi's letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 升奉命久，俟諸軍集，九月始抵隘留關。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng had long borne his commission; waiting for the armies to assemble, he only reached Ailiu Pass in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng had been under orders for months; only after the armies gathered did he reach Ailiu Pass in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 利既與通有成言，乃詭稱陳氏有後，率大小頭目具書詣升軍，乞罷兵，立陳氏裔。

translations.literal: Le Loi, having already come to terms with Tong, falsely claimed that the Chen house had a surviving heir; leading all his chiefs great and small, he submitted a joint petition to Liu Sheng's army begging that hostilities cease and a Chen descendant be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi, already in secret accord with Wang Tong, pretended the Chen line had an heir; with all his chiefs he petitioned Liu Sheng to halt the war and restore a Chen descendant.

sentences.zh: 升不啟封，遣使奏聞。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng did not break the seal; he sent a messenger to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng left the letter unopened and sent a courier to report to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 無何，升進薄倒馬坡，陷歿，後軍相繼盡歿。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Sheng pressed forward to Daomapo, fell into an ambush and perished, and the rear contingents were wiped out one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Sheng pushed on to Daomapo, was ambushed and killed, and the rear guard was destroyed in turn.

sentences.zh: 通聞，懼甚，大集軍民官吏，出下哨河，立壇與利盟誓，約退師。

translations.literal: When Tong heard the news he was terrified; he massed troops, civilians, and officials, went out to the Xia Shao River, raised an altar and swore alliance with Le Loi, agreeing to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified by the news, Wang Tong mustered soldiers and civilians, went to the Xia Shao River, and swore a pact with Le Loi to pull back the army.

sentences.zh: 遂遣官偕賊使奉表及方物進獻。

translations.literal: He then sent officials together with rebel envoys to present a memorial and local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched officials with rebel envoys to submit a memorial and tribute.

sentences.zh: 沐晟軍至水尾，造船將進，聞通已議和，亦引退，賊乘之，大敗。

translations.literal: Mu Sheng's army reached Shuiwei and was building boats to advance; hearing that Tong had already negotiated peace, he too withdrew, and the rebels seized the moment and inflicted a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Sheng's force reached Shuiwei and was preparing boats to advance; learning Wang Tong had already sued for peace, he withdrew too, and the rebels fell on him and routed him.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺進賊與升書，略言：「高皇帝龍飛，安南首朝貢，特蒙褒賞，錫以玉章。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial presented the letter from the rebels to Liu Sheng, which in summary read: "When the August Emperor ascended the throne, Annan was the first to come to court with tribute and was specially honored and rewarded with a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial forwarded Le Loi's letter to Liu Sheng. It said in part: "When the August Emperor took the throne, Annan was first to pay tribute and was honored with a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 後黎賊篡弑，太宗皇帝興師討滅，求陳氏子孫。

translations.literal: Later the Le bandits usurped and murdered; the Taizong Emperor raised an army to suppress and destroy them and sought descendants of the Chen house.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Le usurpers seized power by murder; the Taizong Emperor marched to destroy them and searched for Chen descendants.

sentences.zh: 陳族避禍方遠竄，故無從訪求。

translations.literal: The Chen clan, fleeing disaster, had just fled far away, so none could be found.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen clan had fled far to escape the calamity, and none could be found.

sentences.zh: 今有遺嗣皓，潛身老撾二十年，本國人民不忘先王遺澤，已訪得之。

translations.literal: Now there is a surviving heir, Hao, who hid himself in Laos for twenty years; the people of our state, unforgetting the benevolent legacy of the former king, have traced and found him.
translations.idiomatic: Now a survivor named Chen Hao has been found—he hid in Laos for twenty years, and our people, remembering the old king's grace, have traced him at last.

sentences.zh: 倘蒙轉達黼宸，循太宗皇帝繼絕明詔，還其爵土，匪獨陳氏一宗，實蠻邦億萬生民之幸。

translations.literal: If you would be so kind as to relay this to the imperial throne and follow the Taizong Emperor's edict to continue a broken line and restore his rank and territory, it would be not only the fortune of the Chen clan alone but the blessing of countless millions in this barbarian land.
translations.idiomatic: If this may be conveyed to the throne and the Taizong Emperor's mandate to restore a broken line honored, it would bless not only the Chen house but millions in this frontier realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝得書頷之。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor received the letter he nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor read it and nodded.

sentences.zh: 明日，皓表亦至，稱「臣皓，先王暊三世嫡孫」，其詞與利書略同。

translations.literal: The next day Chen Hao's memorial also arrived, styling himself "Your subject Hao, legitimate grandson of the former king Hue in the third generation"; its wording was much the same as Le Loi's letter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chen Hao's own memorial arrived, calling himself "your subject Hao, legitimate grandson of the former king Hue in the third generation"—much the same as Le Loi's letter.

sentences.zh: 帝心知其詐，欲藉此息兵，遂納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew in his heart it was a fraud but wished to use it to stop the fighting, and so accepted their story.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew it was a ruse but wanted a pretext to stop the war, and accepted the story.

sentences.zh: 初，帝嗣位，與楊士奇、楊榮語交阯事，即欲棄之。

translations.literal: Early on, when the Emperor succeeded to the throne, speaking with Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong about the Jiaozhi affair, he had already wanted to abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: From the start, speaking with Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong about Jiaozhi after his accession, he had wanted to give it up.

sentences.zh: 至是，以表示廷臣，諭以罷兵息民意。

translations.literal: At this point he showed the memorial to the court ministers and instructed them of his intent to cease hostilities and give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now he showed the memorial to the court and explained his wish to stop the war and spare the people.

sentences.zh: 士奇、榮力贊之，惟蹇義、夏原吉不可。

translations.literal: Shiqi and Rong strongly endorsed it; only Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji objected.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and Rong strongly agreed; only Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji dissented.

sentences.zh: 然帝意已決，廷臣不敢爭。

translations.literal: But the Emperor's mind was already made up, and the court ministers dared not contend.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's decision stood, and the ministers did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 十一月朔，命禮部左寺郎李琦、工部右侍郎羅汝敬為正使，右通政黃驥、鴻臚卿徐永達為副使，齎詔撫諭安南人民，盡赦其罪，與之更新，令具陳氏後人之實以聞。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month he appointed Li Qi, Left Secretary of the Ministry of Rites, and Luo Rujing, Vice Minister of Works, as chief envoys, and Huang Ji, Right Commissioner for Transmission, and Xu Yongda, Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, as deputy envoys, to carry an edict reassuring the people of Annan, granting full pardon for their crimes, and giving them a fresh start—ordering them to report in full the truth about any Chen heir.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the eleventh month he named Li Qi and Luo Rujing chief envoys and Huang Ji and Xu Yongda deputies, to carry an edict comforting the people of Annan, pardoning all crimes, and ordering a full report on any Chen heir.

sentences.zh: 因敕利以興滅繼絕之意，並諭通及三司官，盡撤軍民北還。

translations.literal: He also instructed Le Loi in the principle of restoring extinguished states and continuing broken lines, and ordered Tong and the three-commission officials to withdraw all troops and civilians northward.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Le Loi in the principle of restoring a fallen line and ordered Wang Tong and the provincial officials to withdraw every soldier and civilian north.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，通已棄交阯，由陸路還廣西，中官山壽、馬騏及三司守令，由水路還欽州。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Tong had already abandoned Jiaozhi; he returned to Guangxi by land, while the eunuchs Shan Shou and Ma Qi and the three-commission prefects and magistrates returned to Qinzhou by water.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived Wang Tong had already quit Jiaozhi, marching back to Guangxi by land while the eunuchs Shan Shou and Ma Qi and the provincial officials sailed to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 凡得還者止八萬六千人，為賊所殺及拘留者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Of those who made it back there were only eighty-six thousand; those killed or detained by the rebels were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Only eighty-six thousand got out; those killed or held by the rebels were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 天下舉疾通棄地殃民，而帝不怒也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven decried Tong for abandoning territory and bringing calamity on the people, yet the Emperor did not grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: The empire condemned Wang Tong for surrendering the province and ruining the people, but the Emperor did not rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，通等至京，文武諸臣合奏其罪，廷鞫具服，乃與陳智、馬瑛、方政、山壽、馬騏及布政使弋謙，俱論死下獄，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year Tong and the others reached the capital; civil and military officials jointly memorialized their crimes; at court interrogation they fully confessed; Tong together with Chen Zhi, Ma Ying, Fang Zheng, Shan Shou, Ma Qi, and Provincial Commissioner Yi Qian were all sentenced to death and imprisoned, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year Wang Tong and the others reached the capital; officials impeached them jointly, and at trial they confessed. Wang Tong, Chen Zhi, Ma Ying, Fang Zheng, Shan Shou, Ma Qi, and Provincial Commissioner Yi Qian were all sentenced to death, imprisoned, and their estates seized.

sentences.zh: 帝終不誅，長系待決而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor in the end did not execute them; they were simply held long-term awaiting final judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Emperor did not put them to death; they were left in prison awaiting sentence.

sentences.zh: 騏恣虐激變，罪尤重，而謙實無罪，皆同論，時議非之。

translations.literal: Ma Qi's wanton cruelty had provoked the uprising—his guilt was especially heavy—yet Yi Qian was truly innocent; that all received the same sentence drew contemporary criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qi's brutality had helped spark the revolt and his guilt was grave, yet Yi Qian was innocent; sentencing them alike drew widespread criticism.

sentences.zh: 廷臣復劾沐晟、徐亨、譚忠逗留及喪師辱國罪，帝不問。

translations.literal: Court ministers again impeached Mu Sheng, Xu Heng, and Tan Zhong for delay and for the disgrace of losing armies and shaming the state; the Emperor made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers again impeached Mu Sheng, Xu Heng, and Tan Zhong for delay and for losing armies and disgracing the realm, but the Emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 琦等還朝，利遣使奉表謝恩，詭言皓於正月物故，陳氏子孫絕，國人推利守其國，謹俟朝命。

translations.literal: When Qi and the others returned to court, Le Loi sent envoys with a memorial of thanks, falsely reporting that Hao had died in the first month, that the Chen line was extinct, that the people had pressed Le Loi to guard the state, and that he awaited the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi and his party returned, Le Loi sent envoys with thanks, falsely claiming Chen Hao had died in the first month, that the Chen line was extinct, that the people had pressed Le Loi to rule, and that he awaited imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知其詐，不欲遽封，復遣汝敬、永達諭利及其下，令訪陳氏，並盡還官吏人民及其眷屬。

translations.literal: The Emperor also knew it was fraudulent and did not wish to enfeoff him hastily; he again sent Rujing and Yongda to instruct Le Loi and his subordinates to search for the Chen house and to return all officials, civilians, and their dependents.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew the fraud and would not enfeoff him yet; he sent Rujing and Yongda again to tell Le Loi to search for the Chen house and return all officials, civilians, and their families.

sentences.zh: 明年春，汝敬等還，利復言陳氏無遺種，請別命。

translations.literal: The next spring, when Rujing and the others returned, Le Loi again said the Chen had no surviving seed and asked for a separate appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, when Rujing returned, Le Loi again claimed no Chen survivors remained and asked for a separate appointment.

sentences.zh: 因貢方物及代身金人。

translations.literal: He also presented local tribute and a gold figure in lieu of his person.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent local tribute and a gold figure to stand in for himself.

sentences.zh: 又言：「臣九歲女遭亂離散，後知馬騏攜歸充宮婢，臣不勝兒女私，冒昧以請。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Your subject's nine-year-old daughter was scattered in the chaos; I later learned that Ma Qi took her back to serve as a palace maid—I cannot overcome a father's private longing and venture to beg this favor.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "My nine-year-old daughter was lost in the turmoil; I later learned Ma Qi took her back as a palace maid. Overcome by a father's grief, I venture to ask her return.

sentences.zh: 」帝心知陳氏即有後，利必不言，然以封利無名，復命琦、汝敬敕諭再訪，且以利女病死告之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor knew in his heart that even if the Chen had survivors Le Loi would certainly not say so, yet since there was no proper grounds to enfeoff Le Loi, he again ordered Qi and Rujing to instruct him to search once more—and told him that Le Loi's daughter had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor knew Le Loi would never admit any Chen survivor, yet had no grounds to enfeoff him; he sent Qi and Rujing to search again and told Le Loi his daughter had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 五年春，琦等還，利遣使貢金銀器方物，復飾詞具奏，並具頭目耆老奏請令利攝國政。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, when Qi and the others returned, Le Loi sent envoys presenting gold and silver vessels and local goods, again couching his petition in polished language and submitting a memorial jointly from chiefs and elders asking that Le Loi be empowered to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, when Qi returned, Le Loi sent tribute of gold and silver vessels and a polished memorial, with chiefs and elders asking that he be empowered to govern.

sentences.zh: 使臣歸，帝復以訪陳氏裔，還中國遺民二事諭之，詞不甚堅。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, the Emperor again instructed him on the two matters of searching for Chen heirs and returning Chinese people left behind—but his wording was not very firm.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys came back, the Emperor again mentioned searching for Chen heirs and returning Chinese subjects—but without much force.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，利遣使謝罪，以二事飾詞對，復進頭目耆老奏，仍為利乞封。

translations.literal: The next summer Le Loi sent envoys to apologize; he answered the two matters with polished evasions and again submitted a memorial from chiefs and elders still begging enfeoffment for Le Loi.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer Le Loi sent envoys to apologize, evaded both demands with smooth words, and again had chiefs and elders petition for his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 帝乃許之，命禮部右侍郎章敞、右通政徐琦齎敕印，命利權署安南國事。

translations.literal: The Emperor then granted it; he ordered Zhang Chang, Vice Minister of Rites, and Xu Qi, Right Commissioner for Transmission, to carry the edict and seal appointing Le Loi to administer Annan's affairs on a provisional basis.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then agreed and sent Zhang Chang and Xu Qi with an edict and seal appointing Le Loi provisional administrator of Annan.

sentences.zh: 利遣使齎表及金銀器方物，隨敞等入貢。

translations.literal: Le Loi sent envoys bearing a memorial and gold and silver vessels and local goods to enter tribute with Zhang Chang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi sent envoys with a memorial, gold and silver vessels, and tribute to accompany Zhang Chang to court.

sentences.zh: 七年二月達京師，比還，利及使臣皆有賜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year they reached the capital; when they returned, both Le Loi and the envoys received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the second month of the seventh year; on their return Le Loi and his envoys were both rewarded.

sentences.zh: 明年八月來貢，命兵部侍郎徐琦等與其使偕行，諭以順天保民之道。

translations.literal: The next August they came to tribute; Xu Qi and others of the Ministry of War were ordered to travel with their envoys and instruct them in the way of obeying Heaven and protecting the people.
translations.idiomatic: The next August they came to tribute; Xu Qi of the Ministry of War and others were sent with their envoys to instruct them in ruling by Heaven's will and guarding the people.

sentences.zh: 是年，利卒。

translations.literal: That year Le Loi died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Le Loi died.

sentences.zh: 利雖受敕命，其居國稱帝，紀元順天，建東、西二都，分十三道：「曰山南、京北、山西、海陽、安邦、諒山、太原、，明光、諒化、清華、晙安、，順化、廣南。

translations.literal: Although Le Loi had received the imperial commission, within his state he styled himself emperor, adopted the era name Shuntian, established eastern and western capitals, and divided the realm into thirteen circuits: "Shannan, Jingbei, Shanxi, Haiyang, Anbang, Liangshan, Taiyuan, Mingguang, Lianghua, Qinghua, Jun'an, Shunhua, and Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Le Loi had accepted the imperial commission, at home he called himself emperor, took the era name Shuntian, built eastern and western capitals, and divided the country into thirteen circuits: Shannan, Jingbei, Shanxi, Haiyang, Anbang, Liangshan, Taiyuan, Mingguang, Lianghua, Qinghua, Jun'an, Shunhua, and Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 各設承政司、憲察司、總兵使司，擬中國三司。

translations.literal: Each circuit was given an Administrative Commission, a Surveillance Commission, and a Regional Military Commission—modeled on China's three commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit had an administrative commission, a surveillance commission, and a regional military commission—mirroring China's three offices.

sentences.zh: 東都在交州府，西都在清華府。

translations.literal: The eastern capital was at Jiaozhou Prefecture, the western capital at Qinghua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital stood at Jiaozhou Prefecture, the western at Qinghua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 置百官，設學校，以經義、詩賦二科取士，彬彬有華風焉。

translations.literal: He established the full bureaucracy, founded schools, and selected scholars by examinations in classical meaning and poetry and rhapsody—refined, with something of Chinese civilization about it.
translations.idiomatic: He staffed a full bureaucracy, opened schools, and recruited officials by examinations in the classics and poetry— cultivated, with a clear Chinese cast.

sentences.zh: 僭位六年，私諡太祖。

translations.literal: He usurped the throne for six years and posthumously styled himself Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned in all but name for six years and was posthumously styled Taizu.

sentences.zh: 子麟繼，麟一名龍。

translations.literal: His son Lin succeeded; Lin also bore the name Long.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin succeeded him; Lin also went by the name Long.

sentences.zh: 自是其君長皆有二名，以一名奏天朝，貢獻不絕如常制。

translations.literal: From then on each ruler had two names, reporting one name to the Celestial Court; tribute gifts continued without interruption according to the usual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth each ruler kept two names, reporting one to the court; tribute continued on the usual schedule.

sentences.zh: 麟遣使告訃，命侍郎章敞、行人侯璡敕麟權署國事。

translations.literal: Lin sent envoys to announce the bereavement; Vice Minister Zhang Chang and Courier Hou Jin were ordered to instruct Lin to administer state affairs on a provisional basis.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent envoys with news of Le Loi's death; Zhang Chang and Courier Hou Jin were dispatched to authorize Lin as provisional ruler.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使入貢謝恩。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys to enter tribute and express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent envoys to court with tribute and thanks.

sentences.zh: 正統元年四月以宣宗賓天，遣使進香。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Zhengtong 1, on the death of the Xuande Emperor, he sent envoys to offer incense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhengtong 1, on the Xuande Emperor's death, he sent envoys to offer incense.

sentences.zh: 又以英宗登極及尊上太皇太后、皇太后位號，並遣使表賀，貢方物。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys with congratulatory memorials and local tribute for the Yingzong Emperor's accession and the investiture of the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys with congratulations and tribute for the Yingzong Emperor's accession and the elevation of the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 閏六月復貢。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month he sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month he sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 帝以陳氏宗支既絕，欲使麟正位，下廷議，鹹以為宜。

translations.literal: The Emperor, since the Chen clan line was extinct, wished to invest Lin with full rank; the matter was submitted to court deliberation, and all agreed it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chen line was extinct, the Emperor wished to invest Lin fully; the court debated the matter and all agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃命兵部右侍郎李郁、左通政李亨齎敕印，封麟為安南國王。

translations.literal: He then ordered Li Yu, Vice Minister of War, and Li Heng, Left Commissioner for Transmission, to carry the edict and seal and invest Lin as King of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Li Yu and Li Heng with an edict and seal to invest Lin as King of Annan.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使入貢謝恩。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys to enter tribute and express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent envoys to court with tribute and thanks.

sentences.zh: 時安南思郎州土官攻掠廣西安平、思陵二州，據二峒二十一村。

translations.literal: At that time an Annan native official of Silang Prefecture raided Anping and Siling prefectures in Guangxi and seized two mountain vales and twenty-one villages.
translations.idiomatic: An Annan native official of Silang Prefecture then raided Anping and Siling in Guangxi and seized two vales and twenty-one villages.

sentences.zh: 帝命給事中湯鼐、行人高寅敕麟還侵地。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Supervising Secretary Tang Nai and Courier Gao Yin to instruct Lin to return the seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Supervising Secretary Tang Nai and Courier Gao Yin to order Lin to return the seized land.

sentences.zh: 麟奉命，遣使謝罪，而訴安平、思陵土官侵掠思郎。

translations.literal: Lin obeyed the order and sent envoys to apologize, but also complained that the native officials of Anping and Siling had raided Silang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin complied and sent envoys to apologize, but also complained that Anping and Siling officials had raided Silang.

sentences.zh: 帝令守臣嚴飭。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the frontier officials to enforce discipline strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the frontier governors to restrain their men.

sentences.zh: 七年，安南貢使還，令齎皮弁冠服、金織襲衣賜其王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Annan's tribute envoys returned, they were charged to carry leather caps and robes and brocade ceremonial dress as gifts for their king.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Annan's tribute envoys returned, they carried leather caps and robes and brocade court dress for their king.

sentences.zh: 是歲，麟卒，私諡太宗。

translations.literal: That year Lin died and was posthumously styled Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lin died and was posthumously styled Taizong.

sentences.zh: 改元二：紹平六年，大寶三年。

translations.literal: He had two era names: six years of Shaoping and three years of Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: His reign used two era names: six years of Shaoping and three of Dabao.

sentences.zh: 子濬繼，一名基隆，遣使告訃。

translations.literal: His son Jun succeeded—Jun also bore the name Jilong—and sent envoys to announce the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun succeeded—Jun also went by Jilong—and sent envoys with news of the death.

sentences.zh: 命光祿少卿宋傑、兵科都給事中薛謙持節冊封為國王。

translations.literal: Song Jie, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Xue Qian, Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of War section, were ordered to carry credentials and invest him as king.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jie of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Xue Qian, supervising secretary of the Ministry of War, were sent with credentials to invest him as king.

sentences.zh: 濬遣將侵佔城，奪新州港，擄其王摩訶賁該以歸。

translations.literal: Jun sent generals to invade Champa, seized Xinzhou Harbor, captured its king Mohe Bengai, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent troops into Champa, seized Xinzhou Harbor, captured King Mohe Bengai, and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 帝為立新王摩訶貴來，敕安南使，諭濬歸其故王。

translations.literal: The Emperor installed a new king, Mohe Guilai, instructed the Annan envoys, and ordered Jun to return the former king.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor enthroned Mohe Guilai and told Annan's envoys to order Jun to restore the deposed king.

sentences.zh: 濬不奉詔，侵掠人口至三萬三千餘，占城入訴。

translations.literal: Jun disobeyed the edict, seized more than thirty-three thousand people, and Champa came to court to complain.
translations.idiomatic: Jun defied the edict, abducted over thirty-three thousand people, and Champa appealed to the Ming court.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年賜敕戒濬，迄不奉詔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai an admonitory edict was granted to Jun, yet he still would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 the court sent Jun a warning edict; he still refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 四年遣使賀冊立皇太子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he sent envoys to congratulate the investiture of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent envoys to congratulate the crown prince's investiture.

sentences.zh: 天順元年遣使入貢，乞賜袞冕，如朝鮮例，不從。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he sent envoys to tribute, begging investiture with the ceremonial robe and cap as in the Korean precedent; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 his envoys asked for dragon robes and a crown like Korea's; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 其使者乞以土物易書籍、藥材，從之。

translations.literal: His envoys asked to exchange local goods for books and medicines; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys requested books and medicines in exchange for local products; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年遣使賀英宗復辟。

translations.literal: In the second year he sent envoys to congratulate the Yingzong Emperor's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent envoys to celebrate the Yingzong Emperor's restoration.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，其庶兄諒山王琮弑之而自立。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year his elder half-brother, the Prince of Liangshan, Cong, murdered him and usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year his half-brother Liangshan Prince Cong murdered him and seized power.

sentences.zh: 濬改元二：大利十一年，延寧六年。

translations.literal: Jun had two era names: eleven years of Dali and six years of Yanning.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's reign used two era names: eleven years of Dali and six of Yanning.

sentences.zh: 私諡仁宗。

translations.literal: He was posthumously styled Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously styled Renzong.

sentences.zh: 琮，一名宜民，篡位九月，改元天與，為國人所誅，貶厲德侯，以濬弟灝繼。

translations.literal: Cong, who also bore the name Yimin, usurped for nine months, adopted the era name Tianyu, was executed by the people of the state, demoted to Marquis of Lide, and Jun's younger brother Hao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, also called Yimin, ruled nine months under the era Tianyu before his own people killed him; he was demoted to Marquis of Lide and Jun's brother Hao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 灝，一名思誠。

translations.literal: Hao also bore the name Sicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also went by the name Sicheng.

sentences.zh: 初，琮弑濬，以遊湖溺死奏。

translations.literal: At first, when Cong murdered Jun, he reported that Jun had drowned while pleasure-boating on the lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong murdered Jun, he first reported that Jun had drowned on a lake outing.

sentences.zh: 天朝不知，將遣官弔祭。

translations.literal: The Celestial Court did not know and was about to dispatch officials to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming court, unaware, prepared to send officials to mourn and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 琮恐天使至覺其情，言禮不吊溺，不敢煩天使，帝即已之。

translations.literal: Cong feared that when the imperial envoy arrived his crime would be discovered; he said that by ritual one does not offer condolences for drowning and dared not trouble the imperial envoy—the Emperor then dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cong feared an imperial envoy would expose him; he claimed ritual forbade mourning drownings and begged the court not to send one—the Emperor let it drop.

sentences.zh: 使者言濬無子，請封琮。

translations.literal: The envoys said Jun had no son and asked that Cong be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys claimed Jun had no heir and asked that Cong be invested.

sentences.zh: 命通政參議尹旻、禮科給事中王豫往封。

translations.literal: Yin Min, Assistant Commissioner for Transmission, and Wang Yu, Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Rites section, were ordered to go and invest him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Min and Supervising Secretary Wang Yu were dispatched to invest him.

sentences.zh: 未入境，聞琮已誅，灝嗣位，即卻還。

translations.literal: Before entering the border they heard Cong had already been executed and Hao had succeeded; they turned back at once.
translations.idiomatic: Before crossing the border they learned Cong was dead and Hao had succeeded, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 灝連遣使朝貢請封，禮官疑其詐，請命廣西守臣核實奏請，從之。

translations.literal: Hao repeatedly sent envoys to court with tribute begging enfeoffment; the rites officials suspected fraud and asked that Guangxi frontier officials verify and report; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hao repeatedly petitioned for investiture; rites officials suspected fraud and asked Guangxi officials to verify; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 使臣言：「禮，生有封，死有祭。

translations.literal: The envoys said: "By ritual, the living receive enfeoffment and the dead receive sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said, "By ritual the living are enfeoffed and the dead mourned.

sentences.zh: 今濬死既白，請賜祭。

translations.literal: Now that Jun's death has been reported, we beg that sacrifice be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's death is now known— we ask for funeral rites."

sentences.zh: 」乃命行人往祭。

translations.literal: " An courier was then ordered to go and perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent a courier to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 六年二月命侍讀學士錢溥、給事中王豫封灝為國王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Qian Pu, Reader-in-Waiting, and Supervising Secretary Wang Yu were ordered to invest Hao as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year Qian Pu and Supervising Secretary Wang Yu invested Hao as king.

sentences.zh: 憲宗踐阼，命尚寶卿淩信、行人邵震賜王及妃彩幣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, he ordered Chamberlain for Imperial Seals Ling Xin and Courier Shao Zhen to bestow colored silks upon the king and his consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua Emperor took the throne, he sent Ling Xin, Chamberlain for Imperial Seals, and the courier Shao Zhen to grant colored silks to the king and queen.

sentences.zh: 灝遣使來貢，因請冕服，不從，但賜皮弁冠服及紗帽犀帶。

translations.literal: Hao sent envoys to offer tribute and requested full court robes; the request was denied, but he was granted a leather-cap formal dress, a gauze cap, and a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent tribute envoys and asked for full court regalia; the court refused, granting only a leather-cap ensemble, gauze cap, and rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 成化元年八月以英宗賓天，遣使進香，命赴裕陵行禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Chenghua, because the Yingzong Emperor had passed away, envoys were sent to offer incense, and they were ordered to perform rites at the Yuling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chenghua 1, after the Yingzong Emperor's death, envoys were dispatched to offer incense and were instructed to perform rites at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 灝雄桀，自負國富兵強，輒坐大。

translations.literal: Hao was fierce and overbearing; relying on his state's wealth and military strength, he frequently acted with arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was bold and domineering; confident in Annan's wealth and armies, he repeatedly threw his weight about.

sentences.zh: 四年侵據廣西憑祥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he invaded and occupied Pingxiang in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he seized Pingxiang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，命守臣謹備之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he ordered the frontier officials to guard against it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the Emperor ordered frontier officials to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 七年破占城，執其王盤羅茶全，逾三年又破之，執其王盤羅茶悅，遂改其國為交南州，設兵戍守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he defeated Champa, captured its king Panluo Chaan, and more than three years later defeated it again, capturing its king Panluo Chayue; he then renamed the country Jiaonan Prefecture and stationed troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he crushed Champa and took King Panluo Chaan captive; three years later he invaded again, seized King Panluo Chayue, renamed the kingdom Jiaonan Prefecture, and posted a garrison.

sentences.zh: 安南貢道，故由廣西。

translations.literal: Annan's tribute route had traditionally passed through Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Annan's tribute missions had long traveled through Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時雲南鎮守中官錢能貪恣，遣指揮郭景齎敕取其貨。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Neng, the resident eunuch in Yunnan, was greedy and arbitrary; he dispatched Commander Guo Jing bearing an edict to seize goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan resident eunuch Qian Neng was rapacious; he sent Commander Guo Jing with an imperial edict to extort goods.

sentences.zh: 灝素欲窺雲南，遂以解送廣西龍州罪人為詞，隨景假道雲南入京，索夫六百餘，且發兵繼其後，雲南大擾。

translations.literal: Hao had long wished to probe Yunnan; he therefore used the pretext of escorting criminals from Longzhou in Guangxi to the capital, and following Guo Jing took the route through Yunnan to enter the capital, demanding more than six hundred corvée laborers and also sending troops to follow behind—Yunnan was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had long coveted access to Yunnan. Citing the escort of Longzhou convicts to the capital, he followed Guo Jing through Yunnan on the way to Beijing, requisitioned over six hundred bearers, and trailed the party with troops, throwing Yunnan into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 兵部言雲南非貢道，龍州罪人宜解廣西，不必赴京。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War stated that Yunnan was not the tribute route, that Longzhou criminals should be sent to Guangxi for disposal, and need not be brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War replied that Yunnan was not the tribute route, that Longzhou prisoners should be handled in Guangxi, and that they need not be sent to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 乃令守臣檄諭，且嚴邊備。

translations.literal: The court then ordered frontier officials to issue proclamations of instruction and also to tighten border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials were ordered to rebuke Annan by proclamation and tighten border defenses.

sentences.zh: 灝既得憑祥，滅占城，遂侵廣東瓊、雷，盜珠池。

translations.literal: Once Hao had taken Pingxiang and destroyed Champa, he then invaded Qiong and Lei in Guangdong and plundered the pearl fisheries.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized Pingxiang and conquered Champa, Hao raided Qiong and Lei in Guangdong and looted the pearl beds.

sentences.zh: 廣西之龍州、右平，雲南之臨安、廣南、鎮安，亦數告警。

translations.literal: Longzhou and Youping in Guangxi, and Lin'an, Guangnan, and Zhen'an in Yunnan, also repeatedly raised alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou and Youping in Guangxi and Lin'an, Guangnan, and Zhen'an in Yunnan also sent repeated alarms.

sentences.zh: 詔守臣詰之，輒詭詞對。

translations.literal: An edict ordered frontier officials to interrogate him, but he always answered with evasive words.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered frontier officials to demand explanations, but he answered with evasions.

sentences.zh: 廟堂務姑息，雖屢降敕諭，無厲詞。

translations.literal: The court pursued a policy of indulgence; although edicts of instruction were repeatedly issued, there were no stern words.
translations.idiomatic: The court indulged him; though edicts went out again and again, none spoke harshly.

sentences.zh: 灝益玩侮無畏忌，言：「占城王盤羅茶全侵化州道，為其弟盤羅茶悅所弑，因自立。

translations.literal: Hao grew ever more contemptuous and fearless, saying: "King Panluo Chaan of Champa encroached on the route to Huazhou and was murdered by his younger brother Panluo Chayue, who then installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, Hao claimed: "Champa's King Panluo Chaan had encroached on the Huazhou route and was murdered by his brother Panluo Chayue, who then seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 及將受封，又為子茶質苔所弑。

translations.literal: When he was about to receive investiture, he was again murdered by his son Chazhi Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to be invested, he was murdered again by his son Chazhi Tai.

sentences.zh: 其國自亂，非臣灝罪。

translations.literal: The country fell into disorder on its own; this was not the fault of your subject Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Champa had torn itself apart; this was no fault of mine, Hao said.

sentences.zh: 」中朝知其詐，不能詰，但勸令還其土宇。

translations.literal: " The court knew this was deceitful but could not press the matter; it only urged him to restore their territory.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ming court saw through the lie yet could not confront him, urging only that he return the seized lands.

sentences.zh: 灝奏言：「占城非沃壤，家鮮積貯，野絕桑麻，山無金寶之收，海乏魚鹽之利，止產象牙、犀角、烏木、沉香。

translations.literal: Hao memorialized, saying: "Champa is not fertile soil; households rarely store provisions, the wilds lack mulberry and hemp, the mountains yield no gold or treasure, and the sea lacks the profit of fish and salt; it produces only ivory, rhinoceros horn, ebony, and agarwood.
translations.idiomatic: Hao submitted a memorial claiming: "Champa is poor country—few stores in its homes, no mulberry or hemp in the fields, no gold in the hills, no profit from sea salt or fish; only ivory, rhinoceros horn, ebony, and agarwood.

sentences.zh: 得其地不可居，得其民不可使，得其貨不足富，此臣不侵奪占城故也。

translations.literal: To gain its land is not livable, to gain its people is not usable, to gain its goods is not enough to enrich one—this is why your subject did not seize Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Its land could not be settled, its people could not be ruled, its goods could not make us rich—this is why I did not seize Champa, he said.

sentences.zh: 明詔令臣復其土宇，乞遣朝使申畫郊圻，俾兩國邊陲休息，臣不勝至願。

translations.literal: The bright edict orders your subject to restore their territory; I beg that court envoys be sent to mark out the border, so that both countries' frontiers may rest; your subject cannot express his utmost wish more fully.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict commands me to restore their territory; I beg that envoys be sent to demarcate the border so both realms may live in peace—this is my deepest wish.

sentences.zh: 」時占城久為所據，而其詞誕如此。

translations.literal: " Champa had long been occupied by him, yet his words were so absurd.
translations.idiomatic: " Champa had been under his control for years, yet he spoke in this preposterous way.

sentences.zh: 先是，安南入貢，多攜私物，道憑祥、龍州，乏人轉運，輒興仇釁。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Annan came to offer tribute it often carried private goods; passing through Pingxiang and Longzhou, when transport labor was lacking, quarrels were repeatedly provoked.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Annan's tribute missions often carried private merchandise; along the Pingxiang and Longzhou routes, labor shortages repeatedly sparked clashes.

sentences.zh: 會遣使賀冊立皇太子，有詔禁飭之。

translations.literal: When envoys were sent to congratulate the investiture of the crown prince, an edict forbade and admonished this practice.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys were dispatched to congratulate the crown prince's investiture, the court issued an edict forbidding the practice.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，灝遣兵八百餘人，越雲南蒙自界，聲言捕盜，擅結營築室以居。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year, Hao dispatched more than eight hundred troops across the Mengzi border in Yunnan, claiming to hunt bandits, and on their own authority established camps and built houses to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Hao sent over eight hundred soldiers across Yunnan's Mengzi frontier, claiming to pursue bandits, and without permission built camps and houses to occupy.

sentences.zh: 守臣力止之，始退。

translations.literal: Frontier officials forcefully stopped them, and only then did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials forcibly halted them, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 灝既破占城，志意益廣，親督兵九萬，開山為三道，攻破哀牢，侵老撾，復大破之，殺宣慰刀板雅、蘭、掌父子三人，其季子怕雅賽走八百以免。

translations.literal: After Hao had destroyed Champa, his ambitions grew ever wider; he personally commanded ninety thousand troops, opened three routes through the mountains, broke through Ailao, invaded Laos, and again inflicted a great defeat, killing the Pacification Commissioner Daobanya and his sons Lan and Zhang; the youngest son Payasai fled to Baibai to escape.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering Champa, Hao's ambitions swelled; he personally led ninety thousand men, cut three mountain routes, broke through Ailao, invaded Laos, and routed the enemy, killing Pacification Commissioner Daobanya and his sons Lan and Zhang; the youngest, Payasai, fled to Baibai.

sentences.zh: 灝復積糧練兵，頒偽敕于車裏，征其兵合攻八百。

translations.literal: Hao again accumulated grain and trained troops, issued a forged edict in Chelai, and mobilized its forces to join in attacking Baibai.
translations.idiomatic: Hao stockpiled grain, drilled troops, issued a forged edict in Chelai, and summoned its forces to join the assault on Baibai.

sentences.zh: 將士暴死者數千，咸言為雷霆所擊。

translations.literal: Several thousand officers and soldiers died suddenly in the field; all said they had been struck by thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand troops died suddenly in camp; all said lightning had struck them down.

sentences.zh: 八百乃遏其歸路，襲殺萬餘人，灝始引還。

translations.literal: Baibai then blocked their route of retreat and in a surprise attack killed more than ten thousand men; only then did Hao lead his forces back.
translations.idiomatic: Baibai cut off their retreat and ambushed them, killing more than ten thousand; Hao then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝下廷議，請令廣西布政司檄灝斂兵，雲南、兩廣守臣戒邊備而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor submitted the matter to court deliberation; the request was to order the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission to send a proclamation to Hao to withdraw his troops, while Yunnan and the two Guang officials were only to warn and guard the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor referred the matter to court debate; the proposal was that Guangxi's administration commission rebuke Hao and order him to withdraw, while Yunnan and the two Guang provinces need only tighten defenses.

sentences.zh: 既而灝言未侵老撾，且不知八百疆宇何在，語甚誑誕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hao stated that he had not invaded Laos and moreover did not know where Baibai's territory lay; his words were extremely deceitful and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then claimed he had never invaded Laos and did not even know where Baibai lay—outright nonsense.

sentences.zh: 帝復慰諭之，迄不奉命。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent words of reassurance and instruction, yet to the end he did not obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent soothing edicts, but Hao never complied.

sentences.zh: 十七年秋，滿剌加亦以被侵告，帝敕使諭令睦鄰保國。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventeenth year Melaka also reported invasion; the Emperor ordered envoys to instruct them to live in neighborly peace and preserve their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventeenth year Melaka too complained of invasion; the Emperor sent envoys urging neighborly peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，使臣入貢，請如暹羅、爪哇例賜冠帶。

translations.literal: Before long, tribute envoys arrived and requested that caps and belts be granted as in the cases of Siam and Java.
translations.idiomatic: Soon tribute envoys came asking for caps and belts on the same terms as Siam and Java.

sentences.zh: 許之，不為例。

translations.literal: This was granted, but not made a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted once, but not established as precedent.

sentences.zh: 孝宗踐阼，命侍讀劉戩詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, he ordered Reader-in-Waiting Liu Zhan to issue an edict of instruction to that country.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi Emperor took the throne, he ordered Reader-in-Waiting Liu Zhan to proclaim an edict to Annan.

sentences.zh: 其使臣來貢，以大喪免引奏。

translations.literal: When its envoys came to offer tribute, they were exempted from being led in to audience because of the great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Annan's envoys arrived with tribute, they were excused from formal audience because of court mourning.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，時占城王古來以天朝力得還國，復訴安南見侵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi, the Champa king Gulai, having regained his state through the Celestial Court's power, again complained that Annan was invading him.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 3, Champa's King Gulai, restored to his throne with Ming support, again accused Annan of invasion.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書馬文升召安南使臣曰：「歸諭爾主，各保疆土享太平。

translations.literal: Minister of War Ma Wensheng summoned Annan's envoys and said: "Return and instruct your lord: each preserve your territory and enjoy peace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Ma Wensheng summoned Annan's envoys and said: "Tell your king to keep to his borders and live in peace.

sentences.zh: 不然，朝廷一旦赫然震怒，天兵壓境，如永樂朝事，爾主得無悔乎？

translations.literal: Otherwise, should the court one day blaze forth in wrath and celestial troops press upon your borders, as in the Yongle reign—will your lord not regret it?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if the court should one day thunder in anger and imperial armies march to your frontier as in the Yongle era, will your king not rue it?

sentences.zh: 」安南自是有所畏。

translations.literal: " From this Annan came to feel some fear.
translations.idiomatic: " After this Annan showed some restraint.

sentences.zh: 十年，灝卒，私諡聖宗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Hao died and was privately posthumously styled Sheng Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hao died and was privately styled Sheng Zong.

sentences.zh: 其改元二：光順十年，洪德二十八年。

translations.literal: He had two era names: ten years of Guangshun and twenty-eight years of Hongde.
translations.idiomatic: His reign used two era names: ten years of Guangshun and twenty-eight of Hongde.

sentences.zh: 子暉繼，一名鏳，遣使告訃，命行人徐鈺往祭。

translations.literal: His son Hui succeeded—Hui also bore the name Zheng—and sent envoys to announce the bereavement; the courier Xu Yu was ordered to go and perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui succeeded—also called Zheng—and sent envoys with news of the death; the courier Xu Yu was dispatched to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尋賜暉皮弁服、金犀帶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hui was granted a leather-cap dress and a gold rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was soon granted a leather-cap ensemble and a gold rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 其使臣言，國主受王封，賜服與臣下無別，乞改賜。

translations.literal: His envoys stated that the ruler, having received royal investiture, was granted dress no different from his officials, and begged that different gifts be granted.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys complained that the king's investiture robes were no grander than those of his officials and asked for a change of grant.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「安南名為王，實中國臣也。

translations.literal: The ritual officials stated: "Annan is styled king in name, but in fact is a subject of China.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied: "Annan is called king in name but is in truth a subject of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 嗣王新立，必賜皮弁冠服，使不失主宰一國之尊，又賜一品常服，俾不忘臣事中國之義。

translations.literal: When a successor king is newly established, he must be granted a leather-cap formal dress so that he does not lose the dignity of ruling a state, and he is also granted first-rank everyday dress so that he does not forget the duty of serving China as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: A newly enthroned king must receive the leather-cap regalia befitting sovereign dignity, and also first-rank everyday dress reminding him of his subject status.

sentences.zh: 今所請，紊亂祖制，不可許。

translations.literal: The present request would disorder ancestral institutions and cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request would overturn precedent and must be denied.

sentences.zh: 然此非使臣罪，乃通事者導之妄奏，安懲。

translations.literal: Yet this was not the envoys' fault; it was the interpreters who guided them to submit this reckless memorial—how could they be punished?
translations.idiomatic: This was not the envoys' fault but the interpreters' who prompted the improper request—they should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」帝特宥之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor specially pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor granted them special pardon.

sentences.zh: 十七年，暉卒，私諡憲宗，其改元曰景統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Hui died and was privately posthumously styled Xian Zong; his era name was called Jingtong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Hui died and was privately styled Xian Zong; his era name was Jingtong.

sentences.zh: 子氵牽繼，一名敬甫，七月而卒，私諡肅宗。

translations.literal: His son Qian succeeded—Qian also bore the name Jingfu—and died in the seventh month; he was privately posthumously styled Su Zong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian succeeded—also called Jingfu—and died within seven months; he was privately styled Su Zong.

sentences.zh: 弟誼繼，一名璿。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi succeeded—Yi also bore the name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi succeeded—also called Xuan.

sentences.zh: 武宗踐阼，命修撰倫文敘、給事中張弘至詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, he ordered Compiler Lun Wenxu and Supervising Secretary Zhang Hongzhi to issue an edict of instruction to that country.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor took the throne, he ordered Compiler Lun Wenxu and Supervising Secretary Zhang Hongzhi to proclaim an edict to Annan.

sentences.zh: 誼亦遣使告訃，命官致祭如常儀。

translations.literal: Yi also sent envoys to announce a bereavement, and officials were ordered to perform sacrifices according to the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yi too sent envoys announcing a death, and officials were ordered to perform the usual funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 正德元年冊為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 he was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 誼寵任母党阮種、阮伯勝兄弟，恣行威虐，屠戮宗親，鴆殺祖母。
