translations.literal: Yi favored and entrusted his mother's kin, the brothers Ruan Zhong and Ruan Bosheng, who exercised power with cruelty, slaughtered kinsmen of the royal clan, and poisoned his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Yi favored his mother's relatives, the brothers Ruan Zhong and Ruan Bosheng, who ruled brutally, slaughtered royal kinsmen, and poisoned his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 種等怙寵竊權，四年逼誼自殺，擁立其弟伯勝，貶誼為厲湣王。

translations.literal: Zhong and the others, relying on favor to usurp power, in the fourth year forced Yi to kill himself, installed his younger brother Bosheng, and demoted Yi to Prince Li Min.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhong and his faction, abusing imperial favor, forced Yi to suicide, enthroned his brother Bosheng, and demoted Yi to Prince Li Min.

sentences.zh: 國人黎廣等討誅之，立灝孫晭，改諡誼威穆帝。

translations.literal: The countryman Li Guang and others rose to punish and execute them, installed Hao's grandson Chieu, and changed Yi's posthumous title to Weimu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang and others overthrew them, enthroned Hao's grandson Chieu, and restyled Yi as Emperor Weimu.

sentences.zh: 誼在位四年，改元端慶。

translations.literal: Yi reigned four years and adopted the era name Duanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reigned four years under the era Duanqing.

sentences.zh: 晭，一名瀅，七年受封，多行不義。

translations.literal: Chieu, who also bore the name Ying, received investiture in the seventh year and committed many unjust acts.
translations.idiomatic: Chieu, also called Ying, was invested in the seventh year and ruled unjustly.

sentences.zh: 十一年，社堂燒香官陳皓與二子昺、升作亂，殺晭而自立。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chen Hao, incense officer of the She Hall, together with his two sons Bing and Sheng rebelled, killed Chieu, and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chen Hao, a She Hall incense officer, rebelled with his sons Bing and Sheng, killed Chieu, and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 詭言前王陳氏後，仍稱大虞皇帝，改元應天，貶晭為靈隱王。

translations.literal: Falsely claiming descent from the former Chen house, he still styled himself Emperor Dayu, adopted the era name Yingtian, and demoted Chieu to Prince Lingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming Chen descent, he styled himself Emperor Dayu, took the era Yingtian, and demoted Chieu to Prince Lingyin.

sentences.zh: 晭臣都力士莫登庸初附皓，後與黎氏大臣阮私裕等起兵討之。

translations.literal: Chieu's minister, Chief Palace Attendant Mo Dengyong, at first attached himself to Chen Hao, but later joined the Le ministers Ruan Siyu and others in raising troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Chieu's minister Mo Dengyong, Chief Palace Attendant, first backed Chen Hao, then joined Le ministers including Ruan Siyu in arms against him.

sentences.zh: 皓敗走，獲昺及其党陳璲等。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was defeated and fled; Bing and his follower Chen Jin were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao was routed; Bing and his ally Chen Jin were taken.

sentences.zh: 皓與升奔諒山道，據長寧、太原、清節三府自保。

translations.literal: Chen Hao fled with Sheng toward the Lang Son route and held Changning, Taiyuan, and Qingjie prefectures to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao and Sheng fled toward Lang Son and held Changning, Taiyuan, and Qingjie.

sentences.zh: 登庸等乃共立晭兄灝之子譓，改諡晭襄翼帝。

translations.literal: Dengyong and the others then jointly installed Hue, son of Chieu's elder brother Hao, and changed Chieu's posthumous title to Xiangyi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong's faction then enthroned Hue, son of Chieu's elder brother Hao, and restyled Chieu as Emperor Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 晭在位七年，改元洪順。

translations.literal: Chieu reigned seven years and adopted the era name Hongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Chieu reigned seven years under the era Hongshun.

sentences.zh: 譓將請封，因國亂不果。

translations.literal: Hue was about to request investiture, but because the state was in turmoil this did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hue sought investiture, but civil war prevented it.

sentences.zh: 以登庸有功，封武川伯，總水陸諸軍。

translations.literal: Because Dengyong had merit, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Wuchuan and put in overall command of land and water forces.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Dengyong was made Earl of Wuchuan and given command of all land and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 既握兵柄，潛蓄異志。

translations.literal: Once he held military power, he secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: With military power in hand, he began to plot usurpation.

sentences.zh: 黎氏臣鄭綏，以譓徒擁虛位，別立其族子酉榜，發兵攻都城。

translations.literal: The Le minister Zheng Sui, believing Hue merely held an empty throne, separately installed his clansman Youbang and sent troops to attack the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Le minister Zheng Sui, deeming Hue a puppet, set up his kinsman Youbang and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 譓出走，登庸擊破綏兵，捕酉榜殺之，益恃功專恣，遂逼妻譓母，迎譓歸，自為太傅仁國公。

translations.literal: Hue fled; Dengyong defeated Sui's troops, captured Youbang and executed him, relied ever more on his merit to act with arbitrary license, then forced Hue's mother to be his wife, welcomed Hue back, and styled himself Grand Tutor and Duke of Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: Hue fled; Dengyong routed Zheng Sui, captured and killed Youbang, grew bolder with power, forced Hue's mother into marriage, restored Hue to the throne, and took the titles Grand Tutor and Duke of Renguo.

sentences.zh: 十六年率兵攻陳皓，皓敗走死。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he led troops to attack Chen Hao; Hao was defeated, fled, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he attacked Chen Hao, who was defeated, fled, and died.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，登庸自稱安興王，謀弑譓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, Dengyong styled himself Prince of Anxing and plotted to murder Hue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 Dengyong declared himself Prince of Anxing and plotted to kill Hue.

sentences.zh: 譓母以告，乃與其臣杜溫潤間行以免，居於清華。

translations.literal: Hue's mother reported this, and he then, with his minister Du Wenrun traveling by secret routes, escaped and took up residence at Qinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Warned by Hue's mother, he fled with minister Du Wenrun by hidden paths and took refuge at Qinghua.

sentences.zh: 登庸立其庶弟廣，遷居海東長慶府。

translations.literal: Dengyong installed his younger brother Guang and moved him to reside in Changqing Prefecture in Haidong.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong enthroned his younger brother Guang and installed him at Changqing Prefecture in Haidong.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，命編修孫承恩、給事中俞敦詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he ordered Compiler Sun Chengen and Supervising Secretary Yu Dunzhao to issue an edict of instruction to that country.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor took the throne, he ordered Compiler Sun Chengen and Supervising Secretary Yu Dunzhao to proclaim an edict to Annan.

sentences.zh: 至龍州，聞其國大亂，道不通，乃卻還。

translations.literal: When they reached Longzhou, they heard the country was in great turmoil and the route was impassable; they therefore turned back.
translations.idiomatic: At Longzhou they learned Annan was in chaos and the road blocked, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，譓遣使間道通貢，並請封，為登庸所阻。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year Hue sent envoys by secret routes to offer tribute and also to request investiture, but was blocked by Dengyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year Hue sent envoys by hidden routes to tribute and seek investiture, but Dengyong blocked them.

sentences.zh: 明年春，登庸賂欽州判官唐清，為廣求封。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year Dengyong bribed Tang Qing, assistant magistrate of Qinzhou, to seek investiture for Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Dengyong bribed Qinzhou assistant magistrate Tang Qing to petition investiture for Guang.

sentences.zh: 總督張嵿逮清，死於獄。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing arrested Qing, who died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing arrested Tang Qing, who died in custody.

sentences.zh: 六年，登庸令其党危範嘉謨偽為廣禪詔，篡其位，改元明德，立子方瀛為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Dengyong had his follower Wei Fan Jiamo forge an abdication edict from Guang, usurped the throne, changed the era name to Mingde, and installed his son Fang Ying as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Dengyong had his agent Wei Fan Jiamo forge Guang's abdication, seized the throne, adopted the era Mingde, and made his son Fang Ying crown prince.

sentences.zh: 旋鴆殺■，諡為恭皇帝。

translations.literal: He soon poisoned Guang and posthumously styled him Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon poisoned Guang and posthumously styled him Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遣使來貢，至諒山城，被攻而還。

translations.literal: More than a year later he sent envoys to offer tribute; when they reached Lang Son city they were attacked and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he sent tribute envoys; at Lang Son they were attacked and driven back.

sentences.zh: 九年，登庸禪位於方瀛，自稱太上皇，移居都齋、海陽，為方瀛外援，作《大誥》五十九條，頒之國中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Dengyong abdicated in favor of Fang Ying, styled himself Retired Emperor, moved to Duqi and Haiyang to serve as Fang Ying's outside support, composed fifty-nine articles of the Great Admonitions, and promulgated them throughout the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Dengyong abdicated to Fang Ying, styled himself Retired Emperor, moved to Duqi and Haiyang to bolster his son, wrote fifty-nine articles of the Great Admonitions, and issued them nationwide.

sentences.zh: 方瀛改元大正。

translations.literal: Fang Ying changed the era name to Dazheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ying adopted the era Dazheng.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，黎譓卒于清華，國亡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year Hue died at Qinghua, and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: That September Hue died at Qinghua, and the Le dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，皇子生，當頒詔安南。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year a prince was born, and an edict was to be promulgated to Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year, after a prince was born, an edict was to be sent to Annan.

sentences.zh: 禮官夏言言：「安南不貢已二十年，兩廣守臣謂黎譓、黎■均非黎晭應立之嫡，莫登庸陳皓俱彼國纂逆之臣，宜遣官按問，求罪人主名。

translations.literal: Ritual official Xia Yan stated: "Annan has not offered tribute for twenty years; officials of the two Guang say that both Hue and Guang are not the legitimate heirs whom Chieu should have installed; Mo Dengyong and Chen Hao are both usurping rebels of that country; officials should be dispatched to investigate on the spot and seek the names of the guilty principals.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual official Xia Yan argued: "Annan has not tribute for twenty years; Guang officials say neither Hue nor Guang was Chieu's legitimate successor; Mo Dengyong and Chen Hao are usurpers; envoys should investigate and identify the culprits.

sentences.zh: 且前使既以道阻不通，今宜暫停使命。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the previous envoys were already blocked by impassable routes, missions should now be suspended for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Since earlier envoys could not pass, missions should be suspended for now.

sentences.zh: 帝以安南叛逆昭然，宜急遣官往勘，命言會兵部議征討。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing that Annan's rebellion was clear, ordered that officials be urgently dispatched to investigate on the spot, and commanded Yan to confer with the Ministry of War on punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Annan's rebellion plainly, the Emperor ordered an urgent investigation and told Xia Yan to confer with the Ministry of War on military action.

sentences.zh: 言及本兵張瓚等力言逆臣篡主奪國，朝貢不修，決宜致討。

translations.literal: Yan and the minister of war Zhang Zan and others strongly stated that the rebel minister had usurped the ruler and seized the state, tribute was not maintained, and punitive action should certainly be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan and Minister of War Zhang Zan insisted that usurpers had seized the throne, tribute had ceased, and Annan must be punished.

sentences.zh: 乞先遣錦衣官二人往核其實，敕兩廣、雲南守臣整兵積餉，以俟師期，制可。

translations.literal: They begged first to dispatch two officials of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to verify the facts on the spot, and to order frontier officials of the two Guang and Yunnan to gather troops and accumulate provisions in readiness for the campaign; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that two Embroidered Uniform Guard officers verify events on the ground and that Guang and Yunnan officials muster troops and stores pending campaign orders; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃命千戶陶鳳儀、鄭璽等，分往廣西、雲南，詰罪人主名，敕四川、貴州、湖廣、福建、江西守臣，預備兵食，候徵調。

translations.literal: The court then ordered Company Commanders Tao Fengyi, Zheng Xi, and others to go separately to Guangxi and Yunnan to demand the names of the guilty principals, and instructed frontier officials of Sichuan, Guizhou, Huguang, Fujian, and Jiangxi to prepare troops and provisions awaiting mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commanders Tao Fengyi and Zheng Xi were sent to Guangxi and Yunnan to demand the culprits' names, and officials in Sichuan, Guizhou, Huguang, Fujian, and Jiangxi were told to prepare troops and supplies for mobilization.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎唐胄上疏，力陳用兵七不可，語詳其傳中，末言：「安南雖亂，猶頻奉表箋，具方物，款關求入。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Tang Zhou submitted a memorial forcefully setting forth seven reasons why war should not be waged; the details are given in his biography; at the end he stated: "Although Annan is in turmoil, it still frequently submits memorials and letters, presents local products, and knocks at the border gates seeking entry.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Tang Zhou memorialized with seven arguments against war, detailed in his biography; he concluded: "Though Annan is torn by strife, it still sends memorials and gifts and knocks at the border seeking admission.

sentences.zh: 守臣以其姓名不符，拒之。

translations.literal: The frontier officials, because the names did not match, refused them.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier officials turned them away because the names did not correspond.

sentences.zh: 是彼欲貢不得，非負固不貢也。

translations.literal: This meant they wished to offer tribute but could not—it was not that they stubbornly refused tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to tribute but were blocked, not that they willfully withheld tribute.

sentences.zh: 」章下兵部，亦以為然，命俟勘官還更議。

translations.literal: The memorial was forwarded to the Ministry of War, which also agreed, and the court ordered that deliberation resume after the investigation officers returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of War, which concurred; further discussion was ordered once the investigators returned.

sentences.zh: 十六年，安南黎甯遣國人鄭惟僚等赴京，備陳登庸篡弑狀，言：「寧即譓子。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Ninh of Annan sent his countryman Zheng Weiliao and others to the capital, fully setting forth Dengyong's usurpation and regicide, stating: "Ninh is Hue's son.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Le Ninh sent Zheng Weiliao and others to court with a full account of Dengyong's usurpation and murder, saying: "Ninh is Hue's son.

sentences.zh: 譓卒，國人立甯為世孫，權主國事。

translations.literal: When Hue died, the people of the state installed Ninh as heir apparent and entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Hue died, the Annamese installed Ninh as heir and put him in charge of government.

sentences.zh: 屢馳書邊臣告難，俱為登庸邀殺。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent urgent letters to frontier officials reporting his distress, but all were intercepted and killed by Dengyong.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly appealed to frontier officials for help, but Dengyong intercepted and killed every messenger.

sentences.zh: 乞興師問罪，亟除國賊。

translations.literal: He begged that troops be raised to punish the crime and that the state's traitor be speedily removed.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded for a punitive expedition to destroy the usurper at once.

sentences.zh: 」時嚴嵩掌禮部，謂其言未可盡信，請羈之，待勘官回奏，從之。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Song was in charge of the Ministry of Rites; he held that their words could not be fully trusted and asked that they be detained pending the investigators' report; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, then running the Ministry of Rites, doubted their account and asked to detain them until the investigators returned; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋召鳳儀等還，命禮、兵二部會廷臣議，列登庸十大罪，請大振宸斷，克期徂征。

translations.literal: Soon Fengyi and the others were recalled; the Ministries of Rites and War were ordered to confer with court officials, listing Dengyong's ten great crimes and asking that the imperial decision be vigorously applied and a date set for the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi's team was soon recalled; the rites and war ministries convened the court, listed Dengyong's ten crimes, and urged decisive action and a fixed campaign date.

sentences.zh: 乃起右都御史毛伯溫于家，參贊軍務，命戶部侍郎胡璉、高公韶先馳雲、貴、兩廣調度軍食，以都督僉事江桓、牛桓為左、右副總兵，督軍征討，其大將需後命。

translations.literal: Right Censor-in-Chief Mao Bowen was then recalled from retirement to assist in military affairs; Vice Ministers of Revenue Hu Lian and Gao Gongshao were first dispatched to Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two Guang to arrange military provisions; Regional Commanders Jiang Huan and Niu Huan were made left and right deputy commanders-in-chief to supervise the punitive expedition; the commander-in-chief would await later appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen was recalled from retirement as military adviser; Hu Lian and Gao Gongshao were sent ahead to Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guang to mobilize supplies; Jiang Huan and Niu Huan were named deputy commanders pending appointment of a supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 兵部復奉詔，條用兵機宜十二事。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War again received an edict and set forth twelve points on the conduct of the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War then issued twelve operational guidelines under imperial order.

sentences.zh: 獨侍郎潘珍持不可，抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Pan Zhen alone maintained that it should not be done and submitted a forthright memorial in strong remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Vice Minister Pan Zhen dissented, memorializing forcefully against the war.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，褫其職。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor stripped him of office in anger.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督潘旦亦馳疏請停前命，言：「朝廷方興問罪之師，登庸即有求貢之使，宜因而許之，戒嚴觀變，以待彼國之自定。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of the two Guang Pan Dan also hurriedly submitted a memorial asking that the previous order be halted, stating: "Just as the court is raising an army to punish crime, Dengyong already has envoys seeking to offer tribute; the court should take advantage of this to grant permission, maintain strict readiness, watch developments, and await that country's settling itself.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dan, grand coordinator of Guang, urged canceling the campaign: "Even as we mobilize, Dengyong sends tribute envoys; we should accept them, stay on alert, and let Annan settle itself.

sentences.zh: 」嚴嵩、張瓚窺帝旨，力言不可宥，且言黎寧在清都圖恢復，而旦謂彼國俱定，上表求貢，決不可許。

translations.literal: Yan Song and Zhang Zan, divining the Emperor's intent, forcefully argued that pardon was impossible, and further stated that Le Ninh at Qingdu was plotting restoration while Pan Dan claimed that country was settled and petitioned for tribute—a request that must on no account be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Emperor's mind, Yan Song and Zhang Zan insisted there could be no pardon, noting that Le Ninh at Qingdu sought restoration while Pan Dan wrongly claimed Annan was stable and petitioning for tribute—which must be refused.

sentences.zh: 旦疏遂寢。

translations.literal: Pan Dan's memorial was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dan's memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 五月，伯溫至京，奏上方略六事，以旦不可共事，請易之，優旨褒答。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Bowen reached the capital, presented six strategic proposals, said Pan Dan could not work with him, and asked that he be replaced; a gracious edict praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: In May, Bowen reached court with six strategic proposals, declared Pan Dan impossible to work with, and was warmly praised when he asked for a replacement.

sentences.zh: 及兵部議上，帝意忽中變，謂黎寧誠偽未審，令三方守臣從宜撫剿，參贊、督餉大臣俱暫停，旦調用，以張經代之。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of War's deliberations were submitted, the Emperor's intent suddenly shifted midway; he said Le Ninh's truth or falsehood had not yet been determined, ordered frontier officials of the three regions to pacify and suppress as they saw fit, suspended the advisers and grain-supply grand coordinators, transferred Pan Dan to other duties, and replaced him with Zhang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry's plan reached him, the Emperor abruptly reversed course: Le Ninh's claims were unverified; frontier officials should pacify as needed; military advisers and supply chiefs were suspended; Pan Dan was reassigned and Zhang Jing replaced him.

sentences.zh: 時御史徐九皋、給事中謝廷■以修省陳言，亦請罷征南之師。

translations.literal: At the time Censor Xu Jiugao and Supervising Secretary Xie Tingfan, speaking on self-cultivation and austerity, also asked that the southern expedition be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Jiugao and Supervising Secretary Xie Tingfan, in austerity memorials, also called for canceling the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 八月，雲南巡撫汪文盛以獲登庸間諜及所撰偽《大誥》上聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yunnan Grand Coordinator Wang Wensheng reported to the throne the capture of Dengyong's spies and the false Great Admonitions he had composed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Wensheng, Yunnan's grand coordinator, reported capturing Dengyong's spies and a forged Great Admonitions.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，命守臣仍遵前詔征討。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and ordered frontier officials still to follow the previous edict and conduct the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and ordered frontier officials to resume the punitive campaign as previously commanded.

sentences.zh: 時文盛招納黎氏舊臣武文淵得其進兵地圖，謂登庸以可破，遂上之朝。

translations.literal: At the time Wensheng had recruited the Le dynastic old minister Wu Wenyuan and obtained from him a map of routes for advancing troops; he judged Dengyong could be broken and therefore submitted it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng had enlisted Le loyalist Wu Wenyuan, obtained a campaign map, judged Dengyong beatable, and sent both to court.

sentences.zh: 廣東按臣餘光言：「莫之篡黎，猶黎之篡陳，不足深較。

translations.literal: Guangdong Investigating Censor Yu Guang stated: "The Mo usurpation of the Le is like the Le usurpation of the Chen—there is no need to weigh it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong censor Yu Guang argued: "Mo seizing power from Le is like Le seizing it from Chen—not worth dwelling on.

sentences.zh: 但當罪其不庭，責以稱臣修貢，不必遠征，疲敝中國。

translations.literal: One need only punish their failure to attend court, charge them to declare themselves subjects and maintain tribute, and not necessarily launch a distant expedition that would exhaust China.
translations.idiomatic: Punish their absence from court, demand submission and tribute, and spare China a distant war that would drain her strength.

sentences.zh: 臣已遣使宣諭，彼如來歸，宜因以撫納。

translations.literal: I have already dispatched envoys to proclaim the imperial will; if they come to submit, the court should take advantage of this to pacify and accept them.
translations.idiomatic: I have already sent envoys to proclaim the imperial will; if they submit, we should accept and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 」帝以光輕率，奪祿一年。

translations.literal: The Emperor, deeming Guang rash, stripped him of salary for one year.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Yu Guang rash and docked his salary for a year.

sentences.zh: 文盛即傳檄安南，登庸能束身歸命，籍上輿圖，待以不死。

translations.literal: Wensheng then issued a proclamation to Annan: if Dengyong could surrender himself and submit, register and turn over his maps and territories, he would be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng proclaimed to Annan that if Dengyong surrendered and handed over his maps and territories, his life would be spared.

sentences.zh: 於是登庸父子遣使奉表乞降，且投牒文盛及黔國公沐朝輔，具述黎氏衰亂，陳皓叛逆，己與方瀛有功，為國人歸附，所有土地，已載《一統志》中，乞貰其罪，修貢如制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dengyong and his son sent envoys bearing a memorial begging to surrender, and also submitted petitions to Wensheng and the Prince of Qian Mu Chaofu, fully recounting the Le clan's decline and disorder, Chen Hao's rebellion, their own and Fang Ying's merits, and the people's adherence to them; all their lands were already recorded in the Unified Gazetteer; they begged pardon for their crimes and to resume tribute as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong and his son then sent envoys with surrender memorials and petitions to Wensheng and Prince Mu Chaofu of Qian, recounting Le decline, Chen Hao's revolt, their own merits, popular support, and lands already in the gazetteer; they begged pardon and restoration of tribute.

sentences.zh: 朝輔等以十七年三月奏聞，而黎寧承前詔，懼天朝竟納其降，備以本國篡弑始末及軍馬之數、水陸進兵道里來上。

translations.literal: Chaofu and others reported this in the third month of the seventeenth year; meanwhile Le Ninh, following the earlier edict and fearing the Celestial Court would accept the surrender, submitted in full the beginning and end of usurpation and regicide in his country, the numbers of troops and horses, and the routes and distances for advance by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu reported this in the third month of year seventeen; fearing acceptance of the surrender, Le Ninh submitted a full account of usurpation, troop counts, and invasion routes by land and sea.

sentences.zh: 俱下兵部，集廷臣議。

translations.literal: Both submissions were sent to the Ministry of War, which convened court officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Both were referred to the Ministry of War for a court conference.

sentences.zh: 僉言莫氏罪不可赦，亟宜進師。

translations.literal: All said the Mo clan's crimes could not be pardoned and troops should be advanced at once.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed the Mo usurpers were unpardonable and urged immediate advance.

sentences.zh: 請以原推咸甯侯仇鸞總督軍務，伯溫仍為參贊，從之。

translations.literal: They asked that the originally recommended Xianning Marquis Qiu Luan be made overall commander of military affairs, with Bowen continuing as adviser; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They recommended Xianning Marquis Qiu Luan as supreme commander with Bowen as adviser; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 張經上言：「安南進兵之道有六，兵當用三十萬，一歲之餉當用百六十萬，造舟、市馬、制器、犒軍諸費又須七十余萬。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing submitted: "There are six routes for advancing into Annan; the army should number three hundred thousand; provisions for one year should cost 1.6 million; building ships, buying horses, making weapons, and rewarding the army would require more than seven hundred thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing calculated: "Annan has six invasion routes; we need three hundred thousand men, 1.6 million in annual rations, and over seven hundred thousand more for ships, horses, arms, and rewards.

sentences.zh: 況我調大眾，涉炎海，與彼勞逸殊勢，不可不審處也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when we mobilize a great host and cross the hot seas, our labor and their rest are sharply unequal in advantage; this cannot but be carefully weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Massing troops to cross tropical seas puts us at a grave disadvantage against a rested enemy; this must be weighed carefully.

sentences.zh: 」疏方上，欽州知州林希元又力陳登庸可取狀。

translations.literal: Just as the memorial was submitted, Qinzhou Prefect Lin Xiyuan also forcefully set forth reasons why Dengyong could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: As that memorial arrived, Qinzhou Prefect Lin Xiyuan also argued forcefully that Dengyong could be defeated.

sentences.zh: 兵部不能決，復請廷議。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War could not decide and again asked for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War could not decide and sought another court conference.

sentences.zh: 及議上，帝不悅曰：「朕聞卿士大夫私議，鹹謂不當興師。

translations.literal: When the deliberations were submitted, the Emperor was displeased and said: "I hear that you scholar-officials privately discuss matters and all say troops should not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: When the conference report arrived, the Emperor was displeased: "I hear you officials privately agree war is unwise.

sentences.zh: 爾等職司邦政，漫無主持，悉委之會議。

translations.literal: You hold office over state affairs yet have no firm leadership, leaving everything to conference.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the realm's affairs yet offer no leadership, deferring everything to committee.

sentences.zh: 既不協心謀國，其已之。

translations.literal: Since you do not join hearts in planning for the state, let it drop.
translations.idiomatic: Since you cannot unite in service to the state, drop the matter.

sentences.zh: 鸞、伯溫別用。」

translations.literal: Use Luan and Bowen for other duties."
translations.idiomatic: Assign Luan and Bowen elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 十八年冊立皇太子，當頒詔安南。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the crown prince was invested, an edict was to be promulgated to Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, with investiture of the crown prince, an edict was to be sent to Annan.

sentences.zh: 特起黃綰為禮部尚書，學士張治副之，往使其國。

translations.literal: Huang Wan was specially raised to Minister of Rites, with Academician Zhang Zhi as his deputy, to go as envoys to that country.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was specially appointed Minister of Rites, with Academician Zhang Zhi as deputy, to envoy to Annan.

sentences.zh: 命甫下，方瀛遣使上表降，並籍其土地、戶口，聽天朝處分，凡為府五十有三，州四十有九，縣一百七十有六。

translations.literal: As soon as the order was issued, Fang Ying sent envoys submitting a memorial of surrender and registering his lands and population for the Celestial Court to dispose of—altogether fifty-three prefectures, forty-nine subprefectures, and one hundred seventy-six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the order been issued when Fang Ying surrendered, registering lands and population for imperial disposal: fifty-three prefectures, forty-nine subprefectures, and 176 counties.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，下禮、兵二部協議。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this and referred it to the Ministries of Rites and War for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted and referred the matter to the rites and war ministries.

sentences.zh: 至七月，綰猶未行，以忤旨落職，遂停使命。

translations.literal: By the seventh month Wan had still not departed; for disobeying the imperial will he was dismissed from office, and the mission was halted.
translations.idiomatic: By July Wan still had not left; dismissed for defying the throne, the mission was canceled.

sentences.zh: 初，征討之議發自夏言，帝既責綰，因發怒曰：「安南事，本一人倡，眾皆隨之。

translations.literal: At first the punitive expedition had been proposed by Xia Yan; the Emperor, having rebuked Wan, then burst into anger and said: "On the Annan affair, one man initiated it and all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The war had originally been Xia Yan's proposal; after rebuking Wan, the Emperor erupted: "On Annan, one man led and all followed.

sentences.zh: 乃訕上聽言計，共作慢詞。

translations.literal: You then mocked imperial plans and listened to private talk, jointly composing disrespectful words.
translations.idiomatic: You then mocked the throne and traded private counsel, writing insolent memorials together.

sentences.zh: 此國應棄應討，宜有定議，兵部即集議以聞。

translations.literal: Whether this state should be abandoned or punished ought to have a fixed decision; the Ministry of War should immediately convene deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: Whether to abandon or punish Annan needs a firm decision; the Ministry of War must conference and report at once."

sentences.zh: 」於是瓚及廷臣惶懼，請如前詔，仍遣鸞、伯溫南征。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zan and the court officials, in fear, asked as under the previous edict still to dispatch Luan and Bowen on the southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and the terrified court asked, as before, to send Luan and Bowen south.

sentences.zh: 如登庸父子束手歸命，無異心，則待以不死，從之。

translations.literal: If Dengyong and his son surrendered themselves without ulterior intent, they would be spared death; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: If Dengyong and his son surrendered in good faith, their lives would be spared; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 登庸聞，大喜。

translations.literal: When Dengyong heard this, he was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，伯溫等抵廣西，傳檄諭以納款宥罪意。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Bowen and the others reached Guangxi and issued proclamations explaining the intent to accept submission and pardon crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Bowen reached Guangxi and proclaimed amnesty for those who submitted.

sentences.zh: 時方瀛已卒，登庸即遣使請降。

translations.literal: By then Fang Ying had already died, and Dengyong immediately sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ying was already dead; Dengyong at once sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十一月率從子文明及部目四十二人入鎮南關，囚首徒跣，匍匐叩頭壇上，進降表，伯溫稱詔赦之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he led his nephew Wenming and forty-two subordinate officials into Zhennan Pass, with bound heads and bare feet crawled prostrate on the surrender altar, knocked their heads and submitted a surrender memorial; Bowen proclaimed the edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he led his nephew Wenming and forty-two officials into Zhennan Pass, bound and barefoot, crawling to the surrender altar; Bowen proclaimed their pardon.

sentences.zh: 復詣軍門匍匐再拜，上土地軍民藉，請奉正朔，永為籓臣。

translations.literal: They again came to the army headquarters, crawled prostrate and bowed twice, submitted registers of land, troops, and people, and asked to accept the calendar and forever be vassals.
translations.idiomatic: At headquarters they prostrated again, submitted land and population registers, and pledged to accept the calendar and remain vassals forever.

sentences.zh: 伯溫等宣示威德，令歸國俟命。

translations.literal: Bowen and the others proclaimed imperial virtue and ordered them to return to their country and await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen proclaimed imperial mercy and sent them home to await orders.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝大喜，命削安南國為安南都統使司，授登庸都統使，秩從二品，銀印。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered Annan reduced to the Annan Pacification Commission, appointing Dengyong Pacification Commissioner, rank equivalent to vice second rank, with a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and reduced Annan to a Pacification Commission, appointing Dengyong Pacification Commissioner at vice-second rank with a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 舊所僭擬制度悉除去，改其十三道為十三宣撫司，各設宣撫、同知、副使、僉事，聽都統黜陟。

translations.literal: All previously usurped institutions were entirely abolished; its thirteen circuits were changed to thirteen Pacification Offices, each with Pacification Commissioner, Vice Commissioner, Assistant Commissioner, and Registrar, subject to appointment and dismissal by the Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Usurped institutions were abolished; thirteen circuits became thirteen Pacification Offices with standard posts, all subject to the Pacification Commissioner's appointment.

sentences.zh: 廣西歲給《大統曆》，仍三歲一貢以為常。

translations.literal: Guangxi would supply the Great Unified Calendar each year, and tribute every three years would remain the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi would supply the calendar annually; triennial tribute remained the rule.

sentences.zh: 更令核黎寧真偽，果黎氏後，割所據四府奉其祀事，否則已之。

translations.literal: The court further ordered verification of whether Le Ninh was genuine; if he truly was of the Le clan, four prefectures under his control would be granted to maintain sacrificial rites for the dynasty—otherwise the matter would be dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Le Ninh's identity was to be verified; if he was truly Le blood, four prefectures would support his rites—otherwise the offer would lapse.

sentences.zh: 制下，登庸悚惕受命。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, Dengyong received it in fear and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong accepted the decree in fear and trembling.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，登庸卒，方瀛子福海嗣，遣宣撫同知阮典敬等來朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Dengyong died; Fang Ying's son Fuhai succeeded him and sent Pacification Vice Commissioner Ruan Dianjing and others to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Dengyong died; Fuhai, Fang Ying's son, succeeded and sent Ruan Dianjing and others to court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，福海卒，子宏瀷嗣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Fuhai died and his son Honglie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Fuhai died; his son Honglie succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初，登庸以石室人阮敬為義子，封西寧侯。

translations.literal: At first Dengyong had taken Ruan Jing of Shishi as his adopted son and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong had adopted Ruan Jing of Shishi and enfeoffed him Marquis of Xining.

sentences.zh: 敬有女嫁方瀛次子敬典，因與方瀛妻武氏通，得專兵柄。

translations.literal: Jing had a daughter who married Fang Ying's second son Jingdian; through this he also had relations with Fang Ying's wife Lady Wu and came to monopolize military power.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's daughter married Fang Ying's second son Jingdian; through Lady Wu he monopolized military power.

sentences.zh: 宏瀷立，方五歲，敬益專恣用事。

translations.literal: When Honglie was installed, he was only five years old, and Jing grew ever more arbitrary in wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie was only five when enthroned; Ruan Jing grew ever more dictatorial.

sentences.zh: 登庸次子正中及文明避之都齋，其同輩阮如桂、範子儀等亦避居田裏。

translations.literal: Dengyong's second son Zhengzhong and Wenming took refuge at Duqi; their associates Ruan Rugui, Fan Ziyi, and others also withdrew to live in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong's second son Zhengzhong and Wenming withdrew to Duqi; Ruan Rugui, Fan Ziyi, and others retired to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 敬舉兵逼都齋，正中、如桂、子儀等禦之，不勝。

translations.literal: Jing raised troops and pressed Duqi; Zhengzhong, Rugui, Ziyi, and the others resisted but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Jing marched on Duqi; Zhengzhong and the others resisted but were defeated.

sentences.zh: 正中、文明率家屬奔欽州，子儀收殘卒遁海東。

translations.literal: Zhengzhong and Wenming led their families in flight to Qinzhou; Ziyi gathered remnant troops and fled to Haidong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhong and Wenming fled with their families to Qinzhou; Ziyi gathered remnants and escaped to Haidong.

sentences.zh: 敬詭稱宏瀷歿，以迎立正中為詞，犯欽州，為參將俞大猷所敗，誅死。

translations.literal: Jing falsely claimed Honglie had died and, on the pretext of welcoming Zhengzhong to the throne, invaded Qinzhou and was defeated by Regional Vice Commander Yu Dayou, who executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Jing falsely claimed Honglie dead, invaded Qinzhou to install Zhengzhong, was defeated by Yu Dayou, and executed.

sentences.zh: 宏瀷初立時，遣使黎光賁來貢，至南寧，守臣以聞。

translations.literal: When Honglie was first installed he had sent the envoy Le Guangben to offer tribute; when he reached Nanning the frontier officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: At Honglie's accession he had sent Le Guangben to tribute; at Nanning frontier officials reported his arrival.

sentences.zh: 禮官以其國內亂，名分未定，止來使勿進，而令守臣核所當立者。

translations.literal: Ritual officials, because the country was in internal disorder and titles were unsettled, ordered the envoys not to advance and commanded frontier officials to verify who ought to be installed.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials, citing civil war and unsettled succession, barred the envoys and ordered frontier officials to verify the rightful ruler.

sentences.zh: 至三十年事白，命授宏瀷都統使，赴關領牒。

translations.literal: By the thirtieth year the matter was clarified, and the court ordered Honglie appointed Pacification Commissioner and told him to come to the pass to receive his commission.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirtieth year the matter was settled; Honglie was appointed Pacification Commissioner and told to receive his commission at the border pass.

sentences.zh: 會部目黎伯驪與黎甯臣鄭檢合兵來攻，宏瀷奔海陽，不克赴。

translations.literal: Just then Subordinate Official Le Bolí and Le Ninh's minister Zheng Jian combined forces to attack; Honglie fled to Haiyang and could not come to receive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: But Le Bolí and Zheng Jian combined forces against him; Honglie fled to Haiyang and could not come to the pass.

sentences.zh: 光賁等留南寧且十五年，其偕來使人物故大半。

translations.literal: Guangben and the others remained at Nanning for nearly fifteen years; most of those who had come with them died.
translations.idiomatic: Guangben and his party stayed at Nanning nearly fifteen years; most of their companions died.

sentences.zh: 宏瀷祈守臣代請，詔許入京，其都統告身，仍俟宏瀷赴關則給。

translations.literal: Honglie asked frontier officials to petition on his behalf; the court permitted entry to the capital, but his Pacification Commissioner commission would still be given only when Honglie came to the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie asked frontier officials to petition for him; the court allowed Guangben into the capital but withheld the commission until Honglie came to the pass.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，宏瀷卒，子茂洽嗣。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year Honglie died and his son Maoqia succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year Honglie died; his son Maoqia succeeded.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年授都統使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was appointed Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year one he was appointed Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年遣使謝恩，賀即位，進方物，又補累年所缺之貢。

translations.literal: In the third year he sent envoys to thank the court for grace, congratulate the accession, present local products, and also make up tribute owed from accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he sent envoys to thank the court, congratulate the accession, present gifts, and make up years of missed tribute.

sentences.zh: 時莫氏漸衰，黎氏復興，互相構兵，其國益多故。

translations.literal: At the time the Mo clan gradually declined while the Le clan revived; they raised armies against each other, and the state grew ever more troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Mo clan waned as the Le revived; they warred on each other and the realm grew ever more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 始黎甯之據清華也，仍僭帝號，以嘉靖九年改元元和。

translations.literal: When Le Ninh first held Qinghua he still usurped an imperial title and, in the ninth year of Jiajing, changed the era name to Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Le Ninh held Qinghua he still claimed imperial title and in Jiajing year nine adopted the era Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 居四年，為登庸所攻，竄占城界。

translations.literal: After four years he was attacked by Dengyong and fled to occupy the Champa frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Dengyong attacked him and he fled into Champa territory.

sentences.zh: 國人立其弟憲，改元光照。

translations.literal: The people of the state installed his younger brother Xian and changed the era name to Guangzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese installed his brother Xian and adopted the era Guangzhao.

sentences.zh: 十五年廉知寧所在，迎歸清華，後遷于漆馬江。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Lian Zhi knew where Ninh was and welcomed him back to Qinghua; later he moved to Qima River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Lian Zhi located Ninh and restored him to Qinghua; later he moved to Qima River.

sentences.zh: 甯卒，其臣鄭檢立寧子寵。

translations.literal: When Ninh died his minister Zheng Jian installed Ninh's son Chong.
translations.idiomatic: After Ninh died, Zheng Jian installed his son Chong.

sentences.zh: 寵卒，無子，國人共立黎暉四世孫維邦。

translations.literal: When Chong died without sons, the people jointly installed Weibang, fourth-generation descendant of Le Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chong died childless; the people installed Weibang, fourth-generation descendant of Le Hui.

sentences.zh: 維邦卒，檢子松立其子維潭，世居清華，自為一國。

translations.literal: When Weibang died, Jian's son Song installed his son Weitan, who dwelt at Qinghua and constituted a state in himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Weibang died, Zheng Jian's son Song installed Weitan at Qinghua as a separate realm.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十九年，維潭漸強，舉兵攻茂洽，茂洽敗奔嘉林縣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Wanli, Weitan gradually grew strong, raised troops to attack Maoqia, and Maoqia was defeated and fled to Jialin County.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year nineteen Weitan grew strong, attacked Maoqia, and drove him to Jialin County.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，松誘土人內應，襲殺茂洽，奪其都統使印，親黨多遇害。

translations.literal: The next winter Song induced local people to respond from within, launched a surprise attack and killed Maoqia, seized the Pacification Commissioner's seal, and many of his kin were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Song used local collaborators in a surprise attack that killed Maoqia, seized the Pacification seal, and slaughtered many of his kin.

sentences.zh: 有莫敦讓者，奔防城告難，總督陳蕖以聞。

translations.literal: There was one Mo Dunrang who fled to Fangcheng to report the disaster, and Grand Coordinator Chen Qu reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Dunrang fled to Fangcheng to report the crisis; Grand Coordinator Chen Qu informed the court.

sentences.zh: 松復擒敦讓，勢益張。

translations.literal: Song again captured Dunrang and his power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Song captured Dunrang and grew ever more powerful.

sentences.zh: 茂洽子敬恭與宗人履遜等奔廣西思陵州，莫履機奔欽州。

translations.literal: Maoqia's son Jinggong and kinsmen Lvxun and others fled to Silang Prefecture in Guangxi; Mo Lvji fled to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqia's son Jinggong and kin Lvxun fled to Silang in Guangxi; Mo Lvji fled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 獨莫敬邦有眾十余萬，起京北道，擊走黎党範拔萃、范百祿諸軍，敦讓得復歸。

translations.literal: Only Mo Jingbang had a host of more than one hundred thousand; he rose in Jingbei Circuit, routed Le partisans Fan Baocui, Fan Bailu, and other armies, and Dunrang was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mo Jingbang commanded over one hundred thousand men; rising in Jingbei Circuit he routed Le generals Fan Baocui and Fan Bailu, restoring Dunrang.

sentences.zh: 眾乃推敬邦署都統，諸流寓思陵、欽州者悉還。

translations.literal: The masses then pushed Jingbang to act as Pacification Commissioner pro tempore, and all who had fled to Silang and Qinzhou returned.
translations.idiomatic: The people then made Jingbang acting Pacification Commissioner; exiles in Silang and Qinzhou all returned.

sentences.zh: 黎兵攻南策州，敬邦被殺，莫氏勢益衰。

translations.literal: Le troops attacked Nance Prefecture; Jingbang was killed and Mo power declined further.
translations.idiomatic: Le forces attacked Nance Prefecture; Jingbang was killed and Mo power waned further.

sentences.zh: 敬恭、敬用屯諒山高平，敬璋屯東海新安，懼黎兵追索，竄至龍州、憑祥界，令土官列狀告當事。

translations.literal: Jinggong and Jingyong encamped at Gaoping in Langshan; Jingzhang encamped at Xin'an in Donghai; fearing Le pursuit they slipped to the Longzhou and Pingxiang frontier and ordered native officials to submit petitions to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Jinggong and Jingyong held Gaoping in Langshan; Jingzhang held Xin'an in Donghai; fleeing Le pursuit to Longzhou and Pingxiang, they had native officials petition the authorities.

sentences.zh: 維潭亦叩關求通貢，識以國王金印。

translations.literal: Weitan also knocked at the pass seeking to resume tribute, presenting a king's golden seal for identification.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan also came to the pass seeking tribute, presenting a royal golden seal for identification.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣西巡撫陳大科等上言：「蠻邦易姓如弈棋，不當以彼之叛服為順逆，止當以彼之叛我服我為順逆。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Guangxi Grand Coordinator Chen Dake and others submitted: "Barbarian states change surnames like pieces on a chessboard; one should not take their internal rebellion or submission as loyalty or disloyalty—one should only take rebellion against us or submission to us as the measure of loyalty and disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one Chen Dake of Guangxi argued: "Barbarian realms change rulers like chess pieces; their internal strife is not our measure—only rebellion against us or submission to us counts.

sentences.zh: 今維潭雖圖恢復，而茂洽固天翰外臣也，安得不請命而扌間然戮之。

translations.literal: Now although Weitan plots restoration, Maoqia was after all an outer subject of the Celestial Court; how could he be killed without requesting permission?
translations.idiomatic: Weitan may seek restoration, but Maoqia was the court's own vassal—how could he be killed without imperial leave?

sentences.zh: 竊謂黎氏擅興之罪，不可不問。

translations.literal: I venture to say the Le clan's crime of raising troops on their own authority cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: The Le usurpers' crime of unauthorized war, I submit, cannot go unanswered.

sentences.zh: 莫氏孑遺之緒，亦不可不存。

translations.literal: The thread of the Mo house’s remnant line also cannot be allowed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: The Mo clan’s surviving line also had to be preserved.

sentences.zh: 倘如先朝故事，聽黎氏納款，而仍存莫氏，比諸漆馬江，亦不翦其祀，于計為便。

translations.literal: If, following the precedent of earlier reigns, the Le house were allowed to submit while the Mo were still maintained—just as at Qima River their sacrifices were not cut off—the plan would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If, as in earlier reigns, the Le were received while the Mo were left in place—as at Qima River their rites were not extinguished—the arrangement would serve all sides.

sentences.zh: 」廷議如其言。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and agreed with this view.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated and adopted this view.

sentences.zh: 明年，大科方遣官往察，敬用即遣使叩軍門告難，且乞兵。

translations.literal: The next year, as Da Ke was about to dispatch officials to investigate, Jingyong at once sent envoys to knock at the army gate to report distress and beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, before Da Ke could send investigators, Jingyong sent envoys to the military gate pleading distress and begging for troops.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，維潭亦遣使謝罪，求款。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the next year, Weitan also sent envoys to beg forgiveness and seek terms.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn Weitan too sent envoys to apologize and sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 時大科已為兩廣總督，與廣西巡撫戴耀並以屬左江副使楊寅秋，寅秋竊計曰：「不拒黎，亦不棄莫，吾策定矣。

translations.literal: By then Da Ke was governor-general of the two Guang provinces, and Guangxi Surveillance Commissioner Dai Yao together entrusted matters to Left River Vice Commissioner Yang Yinqiu, who secretly calculated: “Neither reject the Le nor abandon the Mo—my plan is settled.”
translations.idiomatic: Da Ke was now governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; with Surveillance Commissioner Dai Yao he left affairs to Vice Commissioner Yang Yinqiu, who decided: “Reject neither Le nor Mo.”

sentences.zh: 」兩遣官往問，以敬恭等願居高平來告，而維潭求款之使亦數至。

translations.literal: He twice sent officials to inquire; Jinggong and the others reported their wish to dwell at Gaoping, while Weitan’s envoys seeking terms also arrived repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yinqiu sent officials twice; Jinggong’s party said they would live at Gaoping, and Weitan’s peace envoys kept coming.

sentences.zh: 寅秋乃與之期，具報督撫。

translations.literal: Yinqiu then fixed a date with them and reported fully to the governor-general and surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yinqiu set terms with both sides and reported to Da Ke and Dai Yao.

sentences.zh: 會敬璋率眾赴永安，為黎氏兵擊敗，海東、新安地盡失，於是款議益決。

translations.literal: When Jingzhang led his followers to Yong’an and was defeated by Le forces, losing Haidong and Xin’an entirely, the decision for a settlement became firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhang marched on Yong’an and was crushed by Le troops, losing Haidong and Xin’an, peace terms were all but settled.

sentences.zh: 時維潭圖恢復名，不欲以登庸自處，無束身入關意。

translations.literal: At that time Weitan, seeking to restore the old name, was unwilling to place himself on Dengyong’s level and had no intention of submitting in person at the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan, claiming restoration, refused to rank himself with Dengyong and would not come to the border in person.

sentences.zh: 寅秋復遣官諭之，其使者來報如約，至期忽言于關吏曰：「士卒饑病，款儀未備。

translations.literal: Yinqiu again sent officials to instruct him; his envoys came reporting as agreed, but when the day arrived they suddenly told the border officers: “The soldiers are hungry and ill, and the ceremonial gifts are not ready.”
translations.idiomatic: His envoys promised compliance, yet on the appointed day told the border guards the army was sick and gifts unready.

sentences.zh: 且莫氏吾仇也，棲之高平，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: “Moreover the Mo are our enemies; housing them at Gaoping—we dare not obey the command.”
translations.idiomatic: “The Mo are our enemies; we dare not accept them at Gaoping.”

sentences.zh: 」遂中宵遁去。

translations.literal: They then fled in the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: They fled at midnight.

sentences.zh: 大科等疏聞，謂其臣鄭松專權所致。

translations.literal: Da Ke and the others memorialized the throne, saying this was caused by his minister Zheng Song’s monopoly of power.
translations.idiomatic: Da Ke reported that Zheng Song’s dominance had caused the flight.

sentences.zh: 維潭復遣使叩關，自己非遁。

translations.literal: Weitan again sent envoys to knock at the pass, declaring that he himself had not fled.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan sent envoys again, denying that he had fled.

sentences.zh: 大科等再遣官諭之，維潭聽命。

translations.literal: Da Ke and the others again sent officials to instruct him, and Weitan obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were sent again, and Weitan submitted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年遣使請期，寅秋示以四月。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he sent envoys to request a date; Yinqiu set the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he asked for a date; Yinqiu named the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 郕期，維潭至關外，譯者詰以六事。

translations.literal: When the day came, Weitan reached the outside of the pass; interpreters questioned him on six points.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan arrived at the pass and was questioned on six counts.

sentences.zh: 首擅殺茂洽，曰：「復仇急，不遑請命。

translations.literal: First, for killing Mao Qia without authorization, he said: “Revenge was urgent; there was no time to request orders.”
translations.idiomatic: On killing Mao Qia he said revenge had brooked no delay.

sentences.zh: 」次維潭宗派，曰：「世孫也，祖暉，天朝曾錫命。

translations.literal: Next, on Weitan’s lineage, he said: “I am the hereditary grandson; my grandfather Hui once received investiture from the Heavenly Court.”
translations.idiomatic: On his lineage he claimed to be the hereditary grandson of Hui, once invested by the court.

sentences.zh: 」次鄭松，曰：「此黎氏世臣，非亂黎氏也。

translations.literal: Next, on Zheng Song, he said: “This is a hereditary minister of the Le house, not one who disturbed the Le.”
translations.idiomatic: On Zheng Song he said he was a hereditary Le minister, not a rebel.

sentences.zh: 」然則何宵遁，曰：「以儀物之不戒，非遁也。

translations.literal: Then why flee at night? He said: “Because the ceremonial objects were not prepared—it was not flight.”
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the midnight flight, he said gifts were unprepared, not flight.

sentences.zh: 」何以用王章，曰：「權仿為之，立銷矣。

translations.literal: Why use royal seals? He said: “They were imitated provisionally and have already been destroyed.”
translations.idiomatic: On royal seals he said they were temporary copies already destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」惟割高平居莫氏，猶相持不絕。

translations.literal: Only on ceding Gaoping to house the Mo did he still hold out without end.
translations.idiomatic: Only on leaving Gaoping to the Mo did he still resist.

sentences.zh: 復諭之曰：「均貢臣也，黎昔可棲漆馬江，莫獨不可棲高平乎？

translations.literal: They again instructed him: “Both are tributary subjects; if the Le could once dwell at Qima River, can the Mo alone not dwell at Gaoping?”
translations.idiomatic: They said: “Both are vassals; if the Le once lived at Qima River, why not the Mo at Gaoping?”

sentences.zh: 」乃聽命。

translations.literal: He then obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He then consented.

sentences.zh: 授以款關儀節，俾習之。

translations.literal: They granted him the ceremonial protocol for submitting at the pass and had him practice it.
translations.idiomatic: He was taught the rites of submission at the pass.

sentences.zh: 維潭率其下入關謁禦幄，一如登庸舊儀。

translations.literal: Weitan led his followers through the pass to bow before the imperial pavilion, exactly as in Dengyong’s former ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan entered the pass and performed the same rites Dengyong had used.

sentences.zh: 退謁寅秋，請用賓主禮，不從，四拜成禮而退。

translations.literal: Withdrawing, he visited Yinqiu and asked for host-and-guest courtesy; this was refused, and he performed four bows and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yinqiu for equal courtesy as host and guest; refused, he bowed four times and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 安南復定。

translations.literal: Annan was settled again.
translations.idiomatic: Annan was pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 詔授維潭都統使，頒曆奉貢。

translations.literal: An edict invested Weitan as Pacification Commissioner and ordered him to receive the calendar and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Weitan was appointed Pacification Commissioner and ordered to receive the calendar and offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 一如莫氏故事。

translations.literal: All followed the former Mo precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement followed the old Mo precedent.

sentences.zh: 先是，黎利及登庸進代身金人，皆囚首面縛，維潭以恢復名正，獨立而肅容。

translations.literal: Earlier, Le Loi and Dengyong, when presenting substitute golden figures, had been bound with heads bowed and faces covered; Weitan, claiming a righteous restoration, stood alone with composed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi and Dengyong had presented bound substitute golden figures; Weitan, claiming restoration, stood upright.

sentences.zh: 當事嫌其倨，令改制，乃為俯伏狀，鐫其背曰：「安南黎氏世孫，臣黎維潭不得蒲伏天門，恭進代身金人，悔罪乞恩。

translations.literal: Those in charge disliked his arrogance and ordered the form changed; he was made to prostrate, and on his back was carved: “Hereditary grandson of the Le house of Annan, your subject Le Weitan, unable to prostrate before the Heavenly Gate, respectfully presents a substitute golden figure, repenting and begging grace.”
translations.idiomatic: Officials deemed him arrogant and made him prostrate; his back was inscribed with a formula of repentance.

sentences.zh: 」自是，安南復為黎氏有，而莫氏但保高平一郡。

translations.literal: From this time Annan again belonged to the Le house, while the Mo kept only Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Annan was Le’s again; the Mo held only Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，維潭卒，子維新嗣，鄭松專其柄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Weitan died; his son Weixin succeeded, and Zheng Song monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Weitan died; Weixin succeeded under Zheng Song’s dominance.

sentences.zh: 會叛酋潘彥構亂，維新與松移保清化。

translations.literal: When the rebel chief Pan Yan stirred trouble, Weixin and Song withdrew to Qinghua.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Yan rebelled, Weixin and Song withdrew to Qinghua.

sentences.zh: 三十四年遣使入貢，命授都統使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year envoys came to court; he was ordered invested Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year tribute envoys came and he was confirmed as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時莫氏宗黨多竄處海隅，往往僭稱公侯伯名號，侵軼邊境，維新亦不能制。

translations.literal: At that time many of the Mo clan’s kinsmen lurked along the coast, often usurping titles of duke, marquis, and earl and raiding the frontier; Weixin could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Mo kinsmen along the coast often styled themselves nobles and raided the border beyond Weixin’s control.

sentences.zh: 守臣檄問，數發兵夾剿，雖應時破滅，而邊方頗受其害。

translations.literal: Frontier officials sent proclamations of inquiry and repeatedly sent troops in pincer attacks; though they were broken at once, the border suffered considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops crushed them repeatedly, yet the frontier still suffered.

sentences.zh: 維新卒，子維祺嗣。

translations.literal: Weixin died and his son Weiqi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Weixin died and Weiqi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，發兵擊莫敬寬，克之，殺其長子，掠其妻妾及少子以歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Tianqi reign, troops were sent against Mo Jingkuan; he was overcome, his eldest son was killed, and his wives and younger son were carried off.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year 4 troops attacked Mo Jingkuan, killed his eldest son, and seized his family.

sentences.zh: 敬寬與次子逃入山中，復回高平，勢益弱。

translations.literal: Jingkuan fled into the mountains with his second son, then returned to Gaoping, his power ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkuan fled to the hills with his second son and returned to weakened Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 然迄明之世，二姓分據，終不能歸一雲。

translations.literal: Yet through the Ming dynasty the two surnames remained divided and could never be reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Ming the two houses remained divided and never reunified.

sentences.zh: 安南都會在交州，即唐都護治所。

translations.literal: The capital of Annan was at Jiaozhou, the seat of the Tang protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Annan’s capital was Jiaozhou, site of the Tang protectorate.

sentences.zh: 其疆域東距海，西接老撾，南渡海即占城，北連廣西之思明、南寧，雲南之臨安、元江。

translations.literal: Its territory reached the sea on the east, bordered Laos on the west, Champa across the sea to the south, and on the north adjoined Siming and Nanning in Guangxi and Lin’an and Yuanjiang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: East to the sea, west to Laos, south across the sea to Champa, north to Guangxi and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 土膏腴，氣候熱，穀歲二稔。

translations.literal: The soil was fertile, the climate hot, and grain ripened twice a year.
translations.idiomatic: The land was rich, the climate hot, and grain yielded two harvests a year.

sentences.zh: 人性獷悍。

translations.literal: The people were by nature fierce and unruly.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce by nature.

sentences.zh: 驩、演二州多文學，交、愛二州多倜儻士，較他方為異。

translations.literal: Huan and Yan Prefectures produced many men of letters; Jiao and Ai Prefectures many men of talent and spirit—unlike other regions.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Yan had many scholars; Jiao and Ai many spirited men—unlike elsewhere.
